docs.text: 1 Run a method Run a method 36 methods Evaluate scIB metrics Plot bubble tables, ranks Run Run a method Run any of 36 integration methods in separate environments. Evaluate Evaluate a run Score a run output with clustering, batch-correction and classification metrics. Plot Plot results Load the stored results and draw bubble tables and rankings. Explore Interactive explorer Browse the full benchmark results in the Shiny explorer. 36 methods, one API Vertical, diagonal, mosaic and cross integration through the multibench API. The methods run in separate environments. scIB metrics Clustering scores (ARI, NMI, ASW, iASW, iF1, cLISI), batch-correction scores (ASW_batch, ARI_batch, NMI_batch, GC, iLISI, kBET) and classification scores (OCA, ACA, Spec, Sens, F1), combined into rank scores per method. Compare methods Rank methods for your data with mtb.recommend, or browse the full rankings in the explorer.

docs.title: scMultiBench
docs.text:
scMultiBench is a benchmark of single-cell multimodal integration methods. The multibench package runs 36 of them from Python and scores their output with the benchmark's metrics. 

pip install multibench-sc

Get started How it works

docs.title: API reference
docs.text: The package is imported as import multibench as mtb. Its functions form four modules, methods, run, metrics and figures, plus a setup group. Each name links to its reference entry, with the parameters and examples.

docs.title: 1. Methods
docs.text:
call returns mtb.find_methods(category, modalities=, needs_labels=) The method ids that fit. mtb.method_info(method) Its env, GPU use, labels, ATAC form, variants and runtime. mtb.params_for(method, category, modalities) What params= can set, with each default. 
import multibench as mtb

mtb.find_methods("vertical", modalities=["rna", "adt"], needs_labels=False)
mtb.params_for("Matilda", "vertical", ["rna", "adt"])["tunable"]

docs.title: 2. Run (Linux)
docs.text:
call returns mtb.scan(dataset, category, methods=, params=) The plan, one row per method: can it run here, why not, and its command. mtb.run(dataset, category, out_dir, methods=, params=) A RunResult, also saved in out_dir. mtb.load_run(out_dir) The RunResult saved in out_dir. mtb.RunResult summary, long, embedding(method), plot(), rescore(), save() and records, one dict per method with its status, parameters, label order and provenance. 
mtb.scan("data/MYCITE", "vertical")
res = mtb.run("data/MYCITE", "vertical", out_dir="out/",
              methods=["Matilda", "totalVI"], params={"Matilda": {"epochs": 10}})
res.summary
emb = res.embedding("Matilda")      # obsm["X_emb"]; obs: each cell's label (and batch)

A dataset is a folder: its path, or its name under mtb.config.data_path. One method is methods=["Matilda"].

docs.title: 3. Metrics
docs.text:
call returns mtb.evaluate(embedding, labels, method=, dataset=, category=) The scores, as the long table. mtb.load_results(category, dataset=) The stored results, as the long table. mtb.recommend(category, long_df=) The overall score and row order of mtb.plot.bubble, best first. mtb.catalog.metrics() The metric codes and their families. 
import pandas as pd

# your run of Matilda on D11, next to the stored results of D11
mine = mtb.evaluate("out/Matilda_D11/embedding.h5", dataset="D11",
                    category="vertical", method="Matilda (this run)")
both = pd.concat([mtb.load_results("vertical"), mine])
mtb.recommend("vertical", long_df=both)

Without labels, evaluate reads the label files of dataset and matches them to the cells by the barcodes run writes into each embedding.h5. In a run folder, the run's record says which method made the file, so method= is only the name of the rows. For an embedding without cell names, the label order is that of method when it names a package method, also as "StabMap (this run)". The stored results are the package's own runs, one dataset per category: D11, D28, D45 and D52.

docs.title: 4. Figures
docs.text:
call returns mtb.plot.bubble(long_df, metrics=, methods=) The article's bubble table. mtb.plot.bar(long_df, metrics=, methods=) One bar per method. 
mtb.plot.bubble(both, metrics="clustering", save="vertical.pdf")

docs.title: Setup
docs.text: call does mtb.io.export_dataset(adata, folder, ...) Writes an AnnData or MuData as a dataset folder. mtb.io.read_canonical(path) Reads a dataset file or an embedding.h5 as an AnnData. mtb.data.fetch(*datasets) Downloads demo datasets and returns each dataset's folder. mtb.data.write_example(dataset) Writes a tutorial's example .h5ad files. mtb.catalog.datasets() The datasets to fetch or with stored results, with their category. mtb.env.install(methods, dry_run=) Installs the methods' envs. dry_run=True shows each env's state and size. mtb.config The settings: data_path, repo_path, envs_dir and leiden_flavor. print(mtb.config) shows them.

docs.title: The long table and metrics=
docs.text:
evaluate, load_results and RunResult.long return the same columns: metric, value, method, dataset, category and source ("stored" or "user") and scored_with. The figures and recommend read any such table. Next to stored results, name your rows apart, such as mine.assign(method=mine.method + " (this run)"), and score them with dataset= of the stored dataset.

metrics= takes a family, a code, or a list of codes and families:

family codes "clustering" ARI, NMI, ASW, iASW, iF1, cLISI "batch" ASW_batch, ARI_batch, NMI_batch, GC, iLISI, kBET "classification" OCA, ACA, Spec, Sens, F1

"all" is the three families, and kBET runs only when named. Higher is better for every metric.

Changes lists the names that 0.4 renamed or removed.

docs.title: Changes
docs.text: What each release adds and changes, newest first. A script written for 0.3 needs the new names in Renamed or removed in 0.4.0. mtb.__version__ is the version you have.

docs.title: New in 0.4.0
docs.text:
• The public API is four modules: methods (find_methods, method_info, params_for), run (scan, run, load_run, RunResult), metrics (evaluate, load_results, recommend, catalog.metrics) and figures (plot.bubble, plot.bar), plus io, data, catalog.datasets, env.install and config.
  • mtb.evaluate returns the long table of load_results, with method= and dataset= naming the rows. Without labels, dataset= reads the dataset's label files, in the cell order of method when it names a package method: its id in any case, its display name, or either followed by a space, such as "StabMap (this run)". A benchmark dataset gives the category; a folder of your own needs category=. Any other name reads the folder's order; a name close to a package method that orders the cells another way gets a did-you-mean warning.
  • run writes the name of each cell into the method's embedding.h5, as the dataset barcodes. evaluate and mtb.io.read_canonical read them, so the scores of a run's file do not depend on method=. For a file of a run folder without them, the folder's run record names the method and the label files it read.
  • RunResult.embedding(method) returns a method's embedding as an AnnData: obsm["X_emb"] in the method's cell order, named by the cells' barcodes (with the label file in front where two files share a barcode), with each cell's label, and its batch when the run had more than one batch. run(batch=) and rescore(batch=, labels=) take these names.
  • mtb.scan returns the plan, one row per method: method, modalities, runnable, reason, env, caveat and command. It takes params=. mtb.run always runs and needs out_dir.
  • mtb.recommend(category, long_df=...) gives the numbers behind a figure, in its row order: method, grand_score, needs_labels, runtime_tier, worst_sec and env. recommend, plot.bar and plot.bubble share one overall score: on each dataset, each value is ranked against the stored rows, so the stored methods keep their scores and order and a row equal to a stored row gets its score.
  • mtb.catalog.datasets() lists the demo subsets too, with a has_results column.
  • metrics= takes one code, such as metrics="ARI", and families inside a list, such as ["clustering", "kBET"]. load_results warns when a code it was given has no stored row.
  • params= values are checked against the choices the script declares: MIRA's acc="banana" is refused before anything runs.
  • A record of run holds scored_by_version, the version that computed its scores, next to multibench_version, the version that ran the method.
  • The scores follow the article's protocol. ARI, NMI, ASW, iASW and iF1 score Leiden clusters searched to the number of cell types; iASW counts every cluster, and iF1 every cell type, as isolated. The new ARI_batch and NMI_batch score Leiden clusters searched to the number of batches. The Leiden backend is leidenalg by default (mtb.config.leiden_flavor).
  • Scores differ from 0.3.x. ARI, NMI and iF1 are usually lower, ASW and iASW higher.
  • The stored results were scored again this way. D11, D28, D45 and D52 were run again. They now hold ARI_batch and NMI_batch for the datasets with several batches, the classification scores (OCA, ACA, Spec, Sens, F1) of D28, D45 and D52, except for a method that writes a graph, and df.attrs["rerun_version"] is 0.4.0.
  • The stored results are the package's own runs only. The published tables leave the API, and the package no longer ships them.
  • One stored dataset per category: D11, D28, D45 and D52. The subsample tables D11s, D28s, D45s and D52s are removed, and so are the Conos rows of D28, a failed run (ARI 0.001), and UINMF's rows of D52, a run on two of its three batches.
  • mtb.env.install installs by default. dry_run=True shows each environment's state and size; its total names a shared layer.
  • The vertical scMM, scMDC, moETM, UnitedNet and iPOLNG read their peaks under the role atac, as every other vertical method. The 0.3 key atac_gas still selects them.
  • mtb.load_run warns once for a folder scored before 0.4.0, and the figures and recommend warn for rows of your own scored before 0.4.0 or without scored_with: res.rescore() scores them as 0.4.0 does.
  • An env with a method env's name counts only when multibench installed it. An env you made yourself is never used, and neither is one that multibench 0.3.9 or older built from a recipe, or 0.3.0 or older unpacked from an archive: rename or remove it, then install again (mtb.env.install(["M"])).
  • An R method reads only the R packages of its env. The personal R library (R_LIBS_USER), R_LIBS, R_LIBS_SITE, ~/.Renviron and ~/.Rprofile are not read. Before, a package there could load instead of the env's copy: MOFA2 stopped with CXXABI_1.3.15 not found.
  • mtb.config is a settings object: a misspelt setting raises, and leiden_flavor takes "leidenalg" or "igraph" when it is set.
  • mtb.io, mtb.env, mtb.catalog and mtb.data hold their public functions only.
  • The install cell of the tutorials asks for multibench-sc>=0.4.0.

docs.title: Behaviour changes in 0.4.0
docs.text:
• mtb.evaluate returns the long table, not the wide frame with a Value column.
  • The source of the stored results is "stored". It was "rerun".
  • mtb.scan returns one row per method: the row that run runs, which leaves out a row inside a larger one (UINMF's two-batch row next to its three-batch row), or the row that says why the method cannot run.
  • mtb.scan of a benchmark dataset takes the dataset's category when none is given: mtb.scan("D11") is vertical.
  • A dataset argument also takes a folder path, such as "mydata/LUNG", relative to the working directory.
  • mtb.io.export_dataset infers atac_kind from the ATAC feature names when it is not given. It raises only when the names do not tell, and it warns when a labels Series without barcodes is matched by position.
  • RunResult.rescore raises FileNotFoundError when it finds the output of no method. Before, it returned a table without scores.
  • RunResult.summary has the columns method, status, the scores, run_sec, caveat and reason. status is scored, ran, failed, skipped or timeout, and reason says why a method has no scores. res.records holds the same statuses (a folder of 0.3 is read with them) and the other fields; reused is True for an output that skip_existing=True reused.
  • RunResult.rescore(metrics=[...]) replaces those scores and keeps the others.
  • run(skip_existing=True) leaves a saved folder without a skipped row for a method that cannot run on this computer, and save keeps the order of the records it merges with.
  • mtb.recommend ranks every metric present by default, as plot.bubble and plot.bar do. With long_df= it lists only the methods of long_df, and it no longer warns about methods without scores.
  • Batch metrics on one batch are refused, as classification is; metrics=None leaves them out.
  • Every route reads an embedding at its own dtype: a float32 embedding.h5 scores the same from its path, an AnnData, res.embedding(m), rescore and run.
  • mtb.evaluate without category= leaves the category column empty.
  • mtb.io.export_dataset warns when a vertical export holds gene-activity ATAC: vertical methods read peaks.
  • mtb.params_for(method) returns the parameters when the method's variants take the same ones, as Matilda's do.
  • mtb.catalog.datasets() lists the datasets mtb.data.fetch downloads or load_results holds, each with its category; it has no simulated or fetchable column.
  • mtb.recommend has no n_datasets, n_datasets_total, coverage and datasets columns.
  • mtb.plot.bar draws the overall score of recommend.
  • mtb.run(skip_existing=True) scores a saved run again, as rescore does, and keeps its record (run_sec, multibench_version, started_at). rescore keeps the label order a record was scored with.
  • mtb.data.fetch(name) returns the dataset's folder.
  • mtb.load_results has the scored_with column of the other long tables.
  • A batch of the wrong length is refused before anything runs.
  • mtb.io.export_dataset refuses peaks given as rna=.
  • On diagonal data, the classification metrics follow the folder's RNA and ATAC sides whatever batch= is.
  • The first metric family of the bubble figure is headed Clustering.
  • mtb.env.install returns a DataFrame: env, methods, state, flavor, archive_bytes and unpacked_bytes. .to_dict("records") gives a list of dicts. An env with one archive for CPU and GPU hosts has the flavor any. Off Linux install raises an error that is an OSError and a RuntimeError.
  • mtb.method_info returns the keys a user reads (id, language, notes, categories, env, atac, needs_labels, supports, runtime, gpu, cpu_params, setup_hint, repo_url, reference). method_info has no tasks, no requires_gpu (gpu == "required") and no n_tunable in supports (params_for).
  • params_for lists the type and the default a run uses of each hyperparameter: no effective key and no script_default. It leaves out the inputs and the values set from the data (scJoint's cty_path1 and input_size, scMDC's nbatch, scMM's model ...), the CUDA switches the package sets per host (device, no_cuda, use_cuda) and arguments the script never reads. params= values are checked against the type the script declares (epochs=2.5 or True is refused), and True/False reach the script as it reads them.
  • recommend and plot.bar refuse rows that repeat a stored method and dataset, as plot.bubble does: rename yours, e.g. rows.assign(method=rows.method + " (this run)").
  • A metric family the stored rows lack, such as classification of your rows, is ranked among your rows and counts in no Overall.
  • Your rows on another dataset than the stored rows are refused: score your embedding with dataset= of the stored dataset.
  • The bubble columns follow catalog.metrics(): ARI, NMI, ASW, iASW, iF1, cLISI.
  • The long tables of evaluate, load_results and RunResult.long have no clustering column.
  • A folder of one batch lists no row for numbered batches (modalities="all" lists them), and mtb.io.export_dataset refuses repeated barcodes.
  • mtb.evaluate(adata) without obsm= takes X_emb; without it, the error names the keys to pass as obsm=.
  • mtb.io.read_canonical reads a method's embedding.h5 into .obsm["X_emb"].
  • When the embedding and the labels or batch both have cell ids, the ids decide. A file or a Series indexed 0..n-1 without cell ids next to an embedding with barcodes is refused: add the barcodes, or pass .to_numpy() to match by position. Ids none of which is a cell are refused too, and ids of other cells next to every cell are left out. A subset of a dataset folder's cells is matched to the folder's label files by its barcodes.
  • evaluate(dataset=) follows the cells of a reordered embedding also where barcodes repeat across batches (D45, D52), named cty2:<barcode> as res.embedding(m) names them. With labels=, a benchmark dataset needs all of its cells, and it gives its category whatever method= is: other cells of yours take a dataset name of their own. Next to a package method that orders the cells otherwise than the folder, labels without cell ids are refused, and labels or a batch with ids follow the method's order.
  • RunResult.rescore(batch=) refuses a batch of the wrong length before anything is scored.
  • run(skip_existing=True) finds a saved run from any working directory.
  • A value of your rows within 1e-6 of the stored value of its own method ("Cobolt (this run)" is Cobolt's) on the same dataset and metric counts as that value in the overall score: re-scoring noise does not move a rank.
  • A stored row is a row of the stored results the package ships: a renamed copy that keeps source == "stored" ranks as your row and moves no stored score.
  • res.embedding(m) of a one-batch dataset has no batch column, so write_h5ad works.
  • mtb.data.write_example returns None. Its printed lines name the files.
  • plot.bar's axis says overall score (D11): your rows can score above 1 or below 0.
  • res.embedding(m) names the cells by the barcodes of the files the method read: scJoint's ATAC cells of D28 by atac_gas.h5. evaluate(dataset=, method=) reads the folder's cells the same way, so such an embedding in any cell order scores as in the method's order. An embedding whose cell ids are not all distinct cells of the folder is refused, not matched by position; the error names the one fix that works.
  • recommend(category, long_df=) refuses rows of another category.
  • An .h5ad that cannot be read is named in one sentence.
  • run(skip_existing=True) with no saved output of the methods in out_dir says so and names the folder it looked for.
  • scan and run say nothing of the rows that read a modality the folder lacks.

docs.title: New in 0.3.9
docs.text:
• The code is simpler inside and about 14% shorter. The functions, their arguments, the messages and the results are those of 0.3.8, except for the changes below.
  • mtb.io.export_dataset and multibench convert stop when labels or a batch column come from cells whose names repeat, in another order than the exported RNA cells. Before, they were written in their own order, so a row could label another RNA cell. The error reads, for example: The cell names of mdata['atac'].obs are not unique, so its labels cannot be matched to the cells. Give each cell a unique name, the same in every modality, first.
  • multibench convert in dataset mode (--rna, --adt, --atac, --atac-from, --labels, ...) says when a file it reads is already a canonical .h5 file. Before, it said the file had no dataset matrix/data. When copying the file is the whole export, the message gives the command that copies it into the folder. Otherwise it says: Pass the .h5ad or .h5mu it came from.
  • The error of mtb.sweep for a parameter the method does not have no longer ends with a sentence about an empty set.
  • When the bubble figure finds repeated rows, it counts a row as stored only when its source is published or rerun, as everywhere else. Before, a source such as rerun_mine also counted.
  • The install cell of the tutorials asks for multibench-sc>=0.3.9.

docs.title: New in 0.3.8
docs.text:
• Classification is added. mtb.classify predicts the cell type of each query cell. Each batch in turn is the reference, as in the article: a small neural network learns the cell types of its cells and predicts the cells of the other batches.
  • mtb.classification_metrics scores the predictions: OCA, ACA, Spec, Sens and F1.
  • On data in two or more batches, evaluate and run_all add these five scores. Vertical data do not get them by default.
  • metrics="classification" selects these five scores.
  • mtb.catalog.metrics() describes the five scores.
  • The bubble figure has a pink Classification block.
  • The stored result tables have no classification scores.
  • The install cell of the tutorials asks for multibench-sc>=0.3.8.

docs.title: New in 0.3.7
docs.text:
• The method environments are smaller to download. All 24 environments are 53.5 GB on a computer with a GPU. In 0.3.6, 26 environments were 82.5 GB.
  • Six environments use torch 2.8.0: scmb_torch, scmb_torch_v2, scmb_cobolt3, scmb_multigrate2, scmb_multivi and scmb_scjoint. Their torch and CUDA libraries are now one download of 3.9 GB, torch-2.8.0-cu12-py39. It is downloaded with the first of these environments and shared by the others. On disk the six take 17.5 GB instead of 49.3 GB.
  • multibench env plan and the dry run of multibench env install --packed add this download once to their total. A last line names it.
  • scMDC and sciCAN run in scmb_torch. The environments scmb_scmdc and scmb_scican are no longer used. You can delete them.
  • A download that gets a server error (HTTP 500 to 599) is tried again, up to four times.
  • The install cell of the tutorials asks for multibench-sc>=0.3.7.

docs.title: New in 0.3.6
docs.text:
• The bubble figure has no L badge and no note lines under its legends. Warnings still name the grey columns and the missing metrics.
  • A method with no score in a metric family gets no Overall bar there. Before, it could get a full bar.
  • Tied ranks share one circle size.
  • Figures no longer depend on matplotlib's rcParams. A figure drawn after mtb.evaluate looks the same as one drawn before.
  • Matilda accepts every parameter of its parameter file in mtb.run(params=...), such as batch_size.
  • scMoMaT reads no label file in mosaic runs. Its needs_labels is False in every category.
  • multibench evaluate --name no longer writes a needs_labels column.
  • The install cell of the tutorials asks for multibench-sc>=0.3.6.

docs.title: New in 0.3.5
docs.text:
• The section "Your own data" of each task tutorial starts from your own .h5ad files. It reads them, writes a dataset folder, checks the folder and runs the methods on it. The install cell of the tutorials asks for multibench-sc>=0.3.5.
  • mtb.data.write_example(dataset) writes the example files that this section reads, so that the notebook runs before your own files are in place. It prints one line per file. A file of your own with one of those names is left as it is.
  • Four recipes for your own data cover other starting points: a 10x .h5 file, labels in a CSV file, no labels and another number of donors.
  • mtb.scan(..., per_method=True) returns one row per method, with the columns method, runnable and reason. It prints what the folder holds and how many cells each matrix file has. It needs a category.
  • mtb.scan(..., modalities="all") and mtb.run_all(..., modalities="all") list every variant of the category, as 0.3.4 did by default. multibench scan --modalities all and multibench run-all --modalities all do the same.
  • The table of mtb.scan has three attrs keys: held, the modalities the folder holds, not_listed, the number of rows left out, and not_held, the modalities those rows lack. With per_method=True it has a fourth, cells, the number of cells of each matrix file.
  • mtb.evaluate(..., missing_labels="drop") scores the labelled cells only. A UserWarning says how many it scored. The attrs of the result hold cells_scored and cells_total, and the scored_with column of mtb.to_long ends with them, such as 270 of 300 cells. multibench evaluate --missing-labels drop does the same.
  • mtb.io.export_dataset(..., batch_index=N, n_batches=M) says how many batches the data has. A file of a higher batch number in the folder is then refused. multibench convert --n-batches M does the same.
  • A column of the object you pass is named "obs:<column>" or "<column>". mtb.io.export_dataset and mtb.evaluate take both, for labels= and for batch=. In 0.3.4, export_dataset took only the first and evaluate only the second. mtb.evaluate(..., clustering="obs:leiden") works too. run_all and rescore are given a folder, not the object, so they take the column itself, such as batch=adata.obs["donor"].

docs.title: Behaviour changes in 0.3.5
docs.text: These changes can stop a 0.3.4 script or change its result. Each entry says what 0.3.4 did.

docs.title: Missing labels and batches
docs.text:
• A label or a batch is missing when it is NaN, None, blank, or text that a label file reads as missing, such as NA, N/A, None, nan and null. The blanks around a text are removed first, so 'NA ' is missing too. A cell type, donor or sample that is really called NA or None needs another name. The messages name the text they found.
  • mtb.evaluate raises ValueError when a cell has no label. 0.3.4 scored the cells without a label as one more cell type, so its scores were wrong. Give every cell a label, or pass missing_labels="drop".
  • mtb.run_all raises ValueError before it runs a method when a label file of the dataset folder has a missing label. 0.3.4 ran the methods and scored the missing label as a cell type. With evaluate=False the methods run without scores. A method that reads the label file as an input, such as Matilda, stops with evaluate=False too: 0.3.4 gave it the missing label as a cell type. mtb.run_all(..., dry_run=True) prints the same fact and raises nothing. multibench run-all exits with 1.
  • BatchResult.rescore records a method that it would score against such a label file as RUN_OK_EVAL_FAILED, with the reason in error and no scores. 0.3.4 scored it. A saved batch_result.json keeps its old scores: rescore returns a new result, and .save() writes it.
  • mtb.io.export_dataset raises ValueError for a label that a label file reads as missing, such as the text NA. 0.3.4 wrote it, and the label file then read back with a missing label. NaN, None and '' raised before.
  • mtb.evaluate(batch=...), mtb.run_all(batch=...) and BatchResult.rescore(batch=...) raise ValueError when a cell has no batch. 0.3.4 counted the cells without a batch as one more batch, so its batch metrics were wrong, without a warning. run_all raises before any method runs, in a dry run too.
  • mtb.io.export_dataset(batch=...) raises ValueError when a cell has no batch. 0.3.4 left the cells with a NaN batch out of the folder and wrote a batch without cells, and it wrote the text nan as a batch of its own.

docs.title: Cell order in evaluate
docs.text:
• mtb.evaluate and multibench evaluate keep the barcodes of an embedding in a .csv or .tsv file whose first column holds them. Labels, batches and clusters that carry barcodes are then matched by barcode, as they are for an .h5ad file. 0.3.4 dropped that column and matched by position, with a warning that the output has no cell ids. A label file in another row order then gave other scores.
  • A label file, batch file or Series in another order than such an embedding is put in the order of the embedding, and a line on stderr says so, such as evaluate: matched labels.csv to the rows of emb.csv by barcode. With verbose=False the line is not printed.
  • When some of the barcodes of the labels, batches or clusters are cells of the embedding and the two do not name the same cells, ValueError gives the number of cells of the embedding that the other file lacks, and one of them. 0.3.4 scored such a call by position when the number of rows was the same.
  • When none of them is a cell of the embedding, the rows are matched by position, with a warning, as in 0.3.4. This is the case when both hold the same cells and the barcodes are written differently, for example without the -1 ending. A label file is matched in the same way for an .h5ad file. A Series with such an index is matched by position for a .csv or .tsv embedding only: for an AnnData it raises ValueError, as in 0.3.4. With another number of rows than the embedding has, the count error follows the warning.
  • An embedding file that repeats a barcode has no cell ids. A label file is then matched by position, with a warning, as in 0.3.4. A Series indexed by barcode raises ValueError for such a file, as it does for an AnnData with repeated obs_names. 0.3.4 matched it by position. Pass labels.to_numpy() to match by position.
  • The first column of the embedding holds barcodes when it holds text: at least one of its values is not a number. A first column of numbers is read as in 0.3.4. Without a header it is left out as row numbers, and with a header it is a column of the embedding. Labels without barcodes are matched by position, as before.
  • The scores of run_all and rescore do not change. The methods write embedding.h5, which holds no cell ids, so the label files are read in file order as before.

docs.title: Dataset folders and exports
docs.text:
• mtb.io.export_dataset and multibench convert raise FileExistsError when the folder holds files of other data that the call does not write. These are matrix files with other cells, label files with another number of labels, and after batch= the files of other batch numbers. A call with batch_index= looks at the files of its own batch number, and at those of a batch number above n_batches=. The call writes nothing, and overwrite=True does not remove these files. 0.3.4 wrote its files next to them, and a method then read both as one dataset. Export to a new folder.
  • A file written for cells that the folder already holds follows the cell order of the files in the folder, and a line on stderr says so. 0.3.4 wrote the rows in the order of the object. Labels added later from an object in another row order then sat on the wrong cells.
  • A call raises ValueError when two matrix files of the folder hold the cells it writes in different orders, and it writes nothing. A diagonal export of RNA and ATAC of the same cells in two orders leaves such a folder. 0.3.4 wrote into it. A paired export without category= replaced both matrix files, which were then in one order. A label file that the diagonal export had written for the ATAC cells kept its old order. A paired export with category="vertical", or a call that wrote one file only, such as the labels, left matrix files of the same cells in two orders, and a method that reads two of them row by row could pair the wrong cells. 0.3.5 refuses both forms. Export this data again in one call, into a new folder.
  • Data with 0 cells raises ValueError. 0.3.4 wrote files without a cell.
  • A matrix with 0 features raises ValueError in export_dataset and to_canonical. 0.3.4 wrote a file without features, for example the ATAC part of a 10x file read without gex_only=False. When the object has a var["feature_types"] column, the message says to check the feature type that was selected. The names are in that column of the object before the split. When Peaks or Antibody Capture is not among them, the 10x file was read without gex_only=False.
  • A matrix whose var["feature_types"] holds more than one type raises ValueError unless a feature filter selects one type. This applies to an AnnData and to an .h5ad file, in export_dataset, to_canonical, multibench convert and the conversion that mtb.run does. The dry run of mtb.run applies the check as the run does. 0.3.4 wrote genes and peaks, or genes and antibodies, into one file, and scan reported the file as present. With 10x type names the message shows the filter to add.
  • A 10x Genomics .h5 file raises ValueError in to_canonical, multibench convert and mtb.run. 0.3.4 handed it on or copied it as a dataset file, which it is not. mtb.io.read_canonical names such a file too. The recipe A 10x .h5 file reads such a file. to_canonical also raises ValueError for another .h5 file whose matrix/data is not 2-D. 0.3.4 returned the path of such a file.
  • export_dataset and to_canonical take ADT from X of an object that also holds obsm entries named X_..., such as X_umap or X_pca. 0.3.4 raised ValueError for any obsm entry, so such a file could not be exported. Another obsm entry still raises, because it may be the protein matrix.
  • mtb.io.export_dataset and multibench convert raise ValueError when two modalities name the same matrix of the same object, such as rna="X", adt="X" or rna="layer:counts", atac="layer:counts", or one object passed for two modalities. The call writes nothing. 0.3.4 wrote the matrix twice: adt.h5, or the ATAC file, was a copy of rna.h5, and no message said so. Pass the second modality as its own object, or name its own place in the object, such as adt="obsm:protein". Two feature filters on one X select two matrices and are written as before.
  • export_dataset raises ValueError when adt_names= is a string. 0.3.4 took each character as one name, so a string with as many characters as the matrix has proteins was written as the protein names. Pass a list, such as adt_names=list(adata.uns["protein_names"]).

docs.title: scan and dry runs
docs.text:
• mtb.scan, mtb.run_all(..., dry_run=True), multibench scan and multibench run-all --dry-run list the variants whose modalities the folder holds. 0.3.4 listed every variant of the category. mtb.scan("D11", "vertical") has 14 rows, where 0.3.4 had 33: D11 holds RNA and ADT, and the 19 rows that read ATAC are left out. The table of 0.3.4 was not wrong. modalities="all", or --modalities all, gives it back. A list of modalities selects as before.
  • Only rows whose input files are missing are left out. The rows with files_ok true are the same, and a real run tries the same methods.
  • The counts follow the listed rows: in the count line of scan, in the dry run, in the No method can run error and in the text of scan --strict. The exit codes of scan --strict are unchanged. The count line says methods when each listed method has one row. On D11 it now reads 14 of 14 methods have their input files.
  • When rows are left out, the count line of scan says so, such as D11 holds RNA and ADT. 19 rows that read ATAC are not listed. modalities="all" lists them. multibench scan prints it on stderr, after the table, and names --modalities all. With verbose=False nothing is printed, and only the attrs keys not_listed and not_held of the table say that rows were left out.
  • A real run_all logs fewer lines. The line N more rows need files this folder does not have. mtb.scan shows them. counts the listed rows only, and a named method that is skipped gets a skipping line for its listed variants only.
  • scan, run_all and inputs_for(check=True) report a 10x Genomics .h5 file under a dataset file name, and a matrix file with 0 features or 0 cells, as a file problem: files_ok is false and the reason names the file. 0.3.4 reported a folder of 10x files named rna.h5 and adt.h5, and a file with 0 features, as present.
  • An ATAC file under a name that no method of the category reads counts as ATAC that the folder holds. A cross folder written with atac_kind="gene_activity" holds atac_gas1.h5, atac_gas2.h5 and so on, and the cross methods read atac1.h5 or atac_peak1.h5. scan lists the rows that read RNA and ATAC for such a folder, and scan(per_method=True) says that it holds RNA and ATAC. None of these rows has its files, so a run tries the same methods as before: none.

docs.title: Messages
docs.text:
• Some errors have a new text and the same exception class. In export_dataset: a labels= or batch= value that names no column, ADT read from X next to an obsm matrix, and batch= in a vertical or diagonal export. The error for a value that names no column lists the columns of obs, five at most. In evaluate, run_all and rescore: the FileNotFoundError for a column name where no column can be looked up. In evaluate: the count error for the label files of one diagonal side, and for a folder without label files. The KeyError for a diagonal side without the label column ends with one more sentence.
  • When that side has other obs columns, the sentence says how to keep the labels. In Python, give the object a column of the same name, such as atac.obs["cell_type"] = atac.obs["predicted.id"]. On the command line, convert each side with its own command and its own --labels, into the same folder. When the side has no obs column, the sentence says to leave labels= out.
  • The warning for values that are not whole numbers follows the argument. For a modality passed as its own object, such as adt=adt, it says to put the raw counts into the X of that object. It gives the line adt.X = adt.layers["counts"] when the object has a layer called counts. For the RNA or the ATAC read from obsm, such as atac="obsm:peaks", it says to name the obsm entry that holds the raw counts. For a feature filter it names the layer with the same filter, such as adt="layer:counts[feature_types=Antibody Capture]". 0.3.4 named adt='layer:counts' or atac='layer:counts' in all three cases. A selector reads the object passed as data, and a layer belongs to its X. So that call wrote a layer of the RNA object as adt.h5 or as the ATAC file, and after a feature filter it wrote the features of every modality. 0.3.5 no longer gives that advice for an object, an obsm entry or a feature filter. The call itself is refused only when another modality names the same matrix, as described under Dataset folders and exports. Otherwise it still passes: see Not solved in 0.3.5.
  • The error for a matrix with several feature types names the types and gives one action, which depends on the type names. With a 10x name among them, Gene Expression, Antibody Capture or Peaks, it shows the filter to add, and it does not say to delete var["feature_types"]: following that advice wrote genes and peaks, or genes and antibodies, into one file. When none of the names is a 10x name, such as protein_coding and lncRNA, the features may all be of one modality. The error then says to delete the column before the export, as del rna.var["feature_types"] for a modality passed as its own object.
  • mtb.io.export_dataset and multibench convert warn when a matrix has a feature name more than once, as the genes of a 10x file can. The names are written as they are, as in 0.3.4, which wrote them without a message. The warning gives the number of repeated names, one of them, and the call that makes them unique: var_names_make_unique() on the object you export, or rna.var_names_make_unique() for a modality passed as its own object. For a feature filter it points to the recipe A 10x .h5 file, which takes the features into their own object first: on the whole object that call also renames an antibody that has the name of a gene. A repeated peak name is not to be renamed: the warning says to keep one column for each peak.
  • mtb.evaluate and multibench evaluate warn when the labels look like a number measured for each cell and not like cell types. There are two signs. With 20 cells or more, there are more distinct labels than half of the cells. Or the labels are numbers and some are not whole numbers. A column such as nCount_RNA given as labels= was scored without a message. The scores are computed as before. The warning names the column or the file, and run_all gives it for the label files of a folder. Cluster numbers and cell-type names give no warning.
  • export_dataset, evaluate and run_all warn when batch= is a Series whose index is the row numbers 0 to n-1 while the cells have barcodes. Such a Series, for example pd.Series(donors), is matched by position, as before, and the warning says to pass a Series indexed by barcode. A column of the object, such as adata.obs["donor"], a list and an array give no warning.
  • multibench evaluate --help says that --labels and --batch can name a column of the obs of an .h5ad output, as celltype or obs:celltype, and that the barcodes of a .csv output are kept.
  • In the reason of scan, numbered ATAC files that the folder holds in the other form share one sentence, such as StabMap needs peak ATAC (atac1.h5, atac2.h5, atac3.h5), and the folder has gene activity (atac_gas1.h5, atac_gas2.h5, atac_gas3.h5). 0.3.4 wrote one sentence per file.

docs.title: Tutorials
docs.text: • Ten tutorials write the folder of their section "Your own data" under a new name, one name per tutorial. MYDIAG became MYDIAG_RNA_ATAC and MYDIAG_BATCHES. MYMOSAIC became MYMOSAIC_RNA_ADT, MYMOSAIC_RNA_ATAC, MYMOSAIC_SHARED and MYMOSAIC_UNSHARED. MYCROSS became MYCROSS_RNA_ADT, MYCROSS_RNA_ATAC, MYCROSS_ADT_ATAC and MYCROSS_TRI. MYCITE, MYMULTIOME and MYTRI are unchanged. In 0.3.4, tutorials that shared a name wrote different layouts into one folder when they ran in the same working directory. The name is now the variable NAME of the export cell, and the check cell and the run cell use it.

docs.title: Not solved in 0.3.5
docs.text:
• The check does not compare the feature names of two batches. scMoMaT takes the features of two batches by position, so the batches need the same genes, proteins and peaks in the same order. export_dataset with batch_index= writes each batch as it is given, and scan reports the folder as complete when its files are there. Compare the var_names of your batches before the export. The mosaic tutorials say so in their section 5.
  • A selector for adt= or atac= that names a layer or the X of the object that holds the RNA writes RNA values as that modality. export_dataset(rna, out, rna="X", adt="layer:counts") writes the layer of the RNA object as adt.h5, and no message says so. For the ATAC, only atac_kind="peak" warns, because gene names do not look like peaks. The two modalities name two matrices there, so the refusal for one matrix named twice does not apply. export_dataset does not compare the features of two modalities. Read a file back with mtb.io.read_canonical and look at its var_names.
  • mtb.io.to_canonical, multibench convert --modality and the conversion of an .h5ad input that mtb.run does write a feature name that occurs more than once without a message of their own. export_dataset warns, and so does multibench convert when it writes a folder. Check with adata.var_names.is_unique.
  • A labels= Series whose index is the row numbers 0 to n-1 is matched by position without a message. Only batch= warns.
  • An export with batch_index= and without n_batches= does not look at the files of other batch numbers. When the folder already holds more batches than your data has, the extra batches stay, and the methods read them. n_batches= finds a batch number above it, not a leftover batch with a lower number. With or without n_batches=, such an export does not look at the files without a batch number either, and an export without batch numbers does not look at the label files that have one. A new folder name avoids all of these.
  • When you change only some of the file names in the read cell of a tutorial, the export writes your cells next to cells of the example, and no error says so. The check cell prints the number of cells of each file. Compare them with your data.
  • Diagonal data with cell types for one side only cannot be scored through run_all. Leave labels= out and pass evaluate=False, as in the recipe No labels. mtb.evaluate(..., missing_labels="drop") scores the labelled side alone there, which does not compare methods.
  • A label file left from other cells is found by its number of labels. One with the same number as your data has cells stays in the folder when the export writes no labels.
  • multibench run-all --dry-run prints nothing about a label file with missing labels. mtb.run_all(..., dry_run=True) prints it, and the run without --dry-run stops.
  • run_all still prints N more rows need files this folder does not have. mtb.scan shows them. in five tutorials: diagonal_rna_atac, diagonal_multi, mosaic_shared, mosaic_unshared and cross_rna_adt_atac. Their folders hold the modalities of variants that need other files.

docs.title: New in 0.3.4
docs.text:
• One tutorial per integration task, for the 13 tasks of the benchmark article: three vertical, two diagonal, four mosaic and four cross. Each tutorial runs two methods on one small dataset that every method of the task runs on, and then on data in your own format. Its last section shows the run of every method of the task, and links a notebook that runs them all.
  • The methods have variants for the tasks that were missing: vertical RNA + ATAC and RNA + ADT + ATAC for more methods, diagonal data in several RNA and ATAC batches, the mosaic patterns [RNA, RNA + ADT, ADT], [RNA, RNA + ATAC, ATAC] and mixed without a shared modality, and cross RNA + ATAC, ADT + ATAC and RNA + ADT + ATAC. mtb.method_info(m)["supports"] lists the variants of a method. The package runs every method that the article evaluates on a task, except Conos on diagonal data in several batches.
  • The package ships six scripts of the benchmark's own runs, for layouts the public scMultiBench repository has no script for: Multigrate on the two mixed mosaic patterns, and UINMF on RNA + ADT + ATAC (vertical, cross and the mixed mosaic pattern with a shared modality) and on three cross batches. run copies them next to the public scripts before it starts.
  • UINMF reads three cross batches of RNA + ADT or RNA + ATAC. It keeps its two-batch variants. On a folder with three batches, such as D52, inputs_for and labels_for now give all three; modalities= selects the two-batch variant.
  • Matilda, scMDC and UnitedNet are listed as reading ATAC peaks, as the benchmark ran them: mtb.method_info(m)["atac"] is "peak". scan and run_all no longer skip them on a peak matrix, and skip them on gene activity instead. Every vertical, mosaic and cross method that reads ATAC now reads peaks.
  • Twelve small datasets for these tutorials: mtb.data.fetchable() lists them. A tutorial's two methods run in minutes.
  • A folder that holds the files of several variants of one method runs the variant with the most modalities, when the others are part of it. A folder with RNA, ADT and ATAC runs the RNA + ADT + ATAC variant. modalities= selects a smaller one.
  • Diagonal data can come in several batches: rna<i>.h5 with atac_gas<i>.h5 or atac_peak<i>.h5, and the labels in rna_cty<i>.csv and atac_cty<i>.csv. mtb.io.export_dataset writes one batch per call with category="diagonal" and batch_index=.
  • A vertical RNA + ATAC folder can hold both atac_peak.h5 and atac_gas.h5. Each method then reads the form it takes.
  • A method that needs a minimum number of cells or genes says so before it runs.
  • An environment installed during a session counts at once, without a restart.
  • The Seurat 5 environment is rebuilt with R 4.4 and is 0.8 GB, down from 2.3 GB.

docs.title: New in 0.3.3
docs.text:
• Method environments download faster. The environments over 2 GiB now come from the GitHub release in parts, instead of from Zenodo.
  • mtb.env.install prints its progress while it downloads, one line per tenth. A dropped or stalled connection resumes where it stopped.
  • cLISI and iLISI now compute on Colab and other Linux hosts with an older glibc. The LISI helper of scib is rebuilt there on first use.
  • The method scripts are fetched without git's per-file progress lines.
  • res.plot() and mtb.plot.bubble show their figure in a notebook without %matplotlib inline.
  • The tutorials install the environments and run the methods, on the demo data and on data written from an AnnData.

docs.title: Commands and flags
docs.text:
• multibench fetch D11 D45 downloads demo datasets. --outputs downloads their stored run-all outputs instead, --scripts the method scripts, and --ref picks a commit or tag of the scripts.
  • multibench config lists the paths in use and where each one comes from. Its scripts_commit row is the commit of the method scripts. With MULTIBENCH_SCRIPTS_REF set, a scripts_ref row says whether it matches. --get data_path prints one value.
  • multibench info METHOD prints what one method needs: environment, GPU use, labels, ATAC input, variants and observed runtimes with cell counts.
  • multibench scan --strict exits with 1 when no requested row is runnable. With --methods, it exits with 1 when any named method has no runnable row. The error counts the blocked rows by cause: missing files, missing environment, no GPU on this computer, wrong ATAC kind, unreadable peak names and scripts not at MULTIBENCH_SCRIPTS_REF. It also exits with 1 while the method scripts are not fetched.
  • multibench scan --assume-gpu and multibench run-all --dry-run --assume-gpu check a GPU-node job from a login node without a GPU.
  • multibench scan --allow-atac-mismatch and multibench run-all --allow-atac-mismatch count a method as runnable when its ATAC file holds the other representation or peak names the method cannot read. The caveat stays.
  • multibench run-all --dry-run runs without --out-dir. Its commands then show <out_dir>.
  • multibench evaluate --leiden-flavor and multibench run-all --leiden-flavor set the Leiden backend of the scoring.
  • multibench run-all --batch CSV gives one batch id per cell, as mtb.run_all(batch=...) does. With --dry-run, a file of the wrong length exits with 1.
  • multibench evaluate --batch-column NAME and multibench run-all --batch-column NAME read the batch from one column of a --batch CSV with several columns, such as a sample sheet. A first column of cell ids still aligns the rows to the cells.
  • multibench evaluate --labels A.csv --labels B.csv stacks several label files in the order given, one batch per file. With --dataset, --category and --method, an order that contradicts the method's cell order exits with 1.
  • multibench evaluate --dataset D --method M --category C without --labels reads the label files of mtb.labels_for. --data-path sets their folder.
  • multibench evaluate --name NAME sets the row name of the long table, such as SCALEX_rerun. With --labels, --method can be left out. A --method given with --name must be a package method. It sets the label order, and a needs_labels column gives the rows the L badge of plot bubble when the method uses labels.
  • multibench convert --overwrite replaces files already in the folder.
  • multibench convert --batch-index N writes one file as batch N of a mosaic or cross dataset.
  • multibench convert --atac-from atac.h5ad --category diagonal reads the ATAC cells from a second file.
  • multibench plot bubble --na warn|skip|raise sets what happens to metrics a method lacks.
  • multibench run --runner "srun --gres=gpu:1 {env_cmd}": {env_cmd} is the command inside the method environment. mtb.run(cmd_template=...) takes it too.

docs.title: Python arguments and settings
docs.text:
• mtb.io.export_dataset(..., overwrite=True) replaces files already in the folder.
  • mtb.io.export_dataset(..., batch_index=N) writes the whole object as batch N of a mosaic or cross dataset.
  • mtb.io.export_dataset(rna, folder, atac=atac, atac_kind="peak", category="diagonal") writes RNA and ATAC from different cells.
  • A selector can end with a feature filter, such as rna="X[feature_types=Gene Expression]". multibench convert takes it too.
  • mtb.scan(..., assume_gpu=True) and mtb.run_all(..., dry_run=True, assume_gpu=True) skip this computer's GPU test.
  • mtb.scan(..., allow_atac_mismatch=True) and mtb.run_all(..., allow_atac_mismatch=True) do what --allow-atac-mismatch does.
  • mtb.labels_for(..., check=True) raises for a vertical or diagonal category on a folder of per-batch files. The default, None, warns.
  • mtb.recommend(..., atac="peak") filters by ATAC representation, as mtb.find_methods does.
  • MULTIBENCH_DATA_PATH and MULTIBENCH_REPO_PATH set data_path and repo_path. MULTIBENCH_SCRIPTS_REF picks a commit or tag of the method scripts. When the scripts present are at another commit, scan marks every row not runnable, run_all raises ValueError before any method starts, and the dry runs print a note. run_all(dry_run=True) prints the note only with verbose=True, as a [run_all] line on stdout after its count line. The config page lists every variable.
  • data_path, repo_path and envs_dir of mtb.config.DEFAULT accept a string.
  • mtb.load_batch(out_dir, data_path=...) says where the dataset folders of a saved result are. A data_path without the dataset folder raises ValueError. Without it, load_batch and rescore look for the dataset folder under the recorded data_path, then under data_root.

docs.title: New fields in results
docs.text:
• RunResult.obs_names holds the cell barcodes of the output rows.
  • RunResult.scripts_commit, env_flavor and hostname record the method scripts, the environment build (cpu, gpu or single) and the computer. Each run_all record in BatchResult.records has them too. A record of a reused output (skip_existing=True) copies them from the earlier record.
  • BatchResult.summary and summary.csv end with a caveat column and a reason column. reason says why a SKIPPED method did not run. Each record in BatchResult.records and batch_result.json has a caveat key. A record saved before 0.3.2 has none, and summary shows NaN there.
  • Each run_all record has data_root, the absolute path of the data folder it used. batch_result.json holds it too. load_batch and rescore write the folder they find into data_path and data_root.
  • run_all(batch=...) and run-all --batch save the batch in out_dir as batch_<hash>.csv. The record key batch_file names the file. BatchResult.save writes it too, also after rescore(batch=...). BatchResult.rescore() reuses that batch, also with labels=. It drops the batch, with a warning, when the dataset folder is not found. For an older result it warns once when metrics= includes a batch metric: pass batch= again to keep the batch metrics.
  • mtb.method_info(m)["gpu"] is required, used when present, not used or unknown.
  • reference_batch in each entry of mtb.method_info(m)["supports"] names a fixed reference batch, such as batch 3 for StabMap in cross.
  • The datasets column of mtb.recommend names the datasets each score comes from.
  • mtb.evaluate(...).attrs holds leiden_flavor, clustering, multibench_version and scib_version.
  • The scored_with column of mtb.to_long records how the scores were computed, such as leidenalg/sweep/0.3.2.

docs.title: Behaviour changes in 0.3.2
docs.text: These changes can stop a 0.3.1 script or change its result.

docs.title: Dataset folders
docs.text:
• mtb.io.export_dataset and multibench convert refuse to replace existing files. FileExistsError lists them. Pass overwrite=True or --overwrite. A failed call writes nothing.
  • category="mosaic" writes ATAC as atac<i>.h5, where 0.3.1 wrote atac_peak<i>.h5. Folders with the old names still work.
  • category="diagonal" pairs no barcodes, so RNA and ATAC may come from different cells. The labels go to rna_cty.csv and atac_cty.csv, not cty.csv.
  • batch= with category="vertical" or "diagonal" raises ValueError. 0.3.1 wrote per-batch files that no vertical method reads.
  • A missing label (NaN, None or '') raises ValueError.
  • RNA, ADT or peak values that are not whole numbers give a UserWarning. The methods expect raw counts.
  • mtb.io.to_canonical(src, folder, modality="gas") into a folder with atac_peak.h5 writes the rows in that file's cell order.

docs.title: File checks
docs.text:
• A vertical folder of per-batch files (rna1.h5, rna2.h5, ...) fails the file check. 0.3.1 read rna1.h5 as rna.h5.
  • Seurat_v5 needs rna.h5 and atac_peak.h5 from the same cells. A folder whose two files hold different cells, D28 included, fails its file check, and run_all skips Seurat_v5 there.
  • mtb.labels_for(..., "Seurat_v5") lists atac_cty before rna_cty, Seurat_v5's cell order.
  • mtb.labels_for(dataset, category, method) returns only the label files of the batches the method reads. UINMF on D52 gets cty1 and cty2, and the caveat of scan and run_all says UINMF reads batches 1-2 of 3. Batch 3 is not used.
  • In a diagonal folder, atac_gas.h5 must hold the cells of atac_peak.h5 in the same order. Otherwise the methods that read atac_gas.h5 fail the file check. Barcodes that differ only in a trailing -<n> count as the same cell.
  • UnitedNet reads cty.csv, where 0.3.1 read rna_cty.csv. inputs_for returns the key cty. A folder with only rna_cty.csv still works, and labels_for(..., "vertical", "UnitedNet") returns that file under cty. The input key rna_cty of mtb.run and multibench run --input still works, with a DeprecationWarning.
  • modalities=["rna", "atac_peak"] selects the methods that read peaks, and "atac_gas" the methods that read gene activity. In 0.3.1, find_methods and recommend returned every RNA+ATAC method for either token.
  • In scan and run_all, "atac_gas" no longer selects moETM, scMM and iPOLNG, which read peaks, unless methods= names them. Pass "atac_peak" for them. "atac_peak" also lists MultiMAP and Seurat_v3, which read both ATAC files.
  • A row whose ATAC file holds the other representation, such as peaks for Matilda, is not runnable in scan, and run_all skips it, also when methods= names the method. allow_atac_mismatch=True or --allow-atac-mismatch runs it with the caveat, as 0.3.1 did.
  • GLUE and Seurat_v3 are not runnable in scan when the peak file holds names without chromosome, start and end, such as peak_1. allow_atac_mismatch=True runs them anyway. 0.3.1 checked only GLUE on D28.

docs.title: Runs
docs.text:
• run_all into an out_dir that holds a saved result of the same dataset and category merges the records. Another dataset or category raises ValueError before any method runs. BatchResult.save does the same.
  • mtb.run(..., dry_run=True) checks the inputs as a real run does. A MuData or .h5mu input raises ValueError. An input file that does not exist gets only a note, such as SCALEX reads data/LUNG/atac_gas.h5, which does not exist.
  • mtb.run and multibench run, dry run included, apply the cell checks of the file check to the files you pass. Seurat_v5 inputs from different cells, or an atac_gas file whose cells differ from atac_peak in set or order, raise ValueError before anything runs.
  • GLUE reads a copy of atac_peak.h5 whose peak names mtb.run rewrites to chr:start-end, as for Seurat_v3. The command column of scan names that copy, which mtb.run writes first. Start GLUE with mtb.run, run_all or multibench run. The printed command alone fails in a job script.
  • mtb.run and multibench run warn once when an ATAC input holds the other representation or peak names the method cannot read, and still run. The dry run prints the same text on a line that starts with #.
  • run_all prints the caveat of each row it runs in its log, in the dry run too.
  • The result lines of run_all and rescore name the ARI, such as ARI 0.629. A FAIL or TIMEOUT line ends with the last line of the error that names a cause.
  • A real run_all logs skipping <method>: <reason> for a method it does not start, and records it with status SKIPPED and the reason in error. This covers each named method with no runnable row and each blocked method whose files are present. failures lists it only when methods= named it. A SKIPPED record never replaces an earlier run of that method in out_dir. When no requested method can start, run_all raises ValueError instead, and multibench run-all exits with 1.
  • scan and run_all, dry run included, raise ValueError before anything runs when methods= names a method with no variant in the category or modalities. 0.3.1 dropped that method. multibench run-all exits with 1.
  • BatchResult.rescore keeps FAIL and TIMEOUT records as they are. 0.3.1 scored them again, and a failed method came back as CHAIN_OK, RUN_OK_EVAL_FAILED or RUN_OK_NO_EMBEDDING.
  • A record that rescore cannot score, RUN_OK_NO_LABEL_MATCH or RUN_OK_EVAL_FAILED, keeps no metrics, batch_source or n_batches from an earlier scoring. 0.3.1 kept the batch columns, and the metrics when the output file could not be read.
  • BatchResult.rescore(metrics=...) with no ARI, NMI or iF1 keeps the stored label order and runs no Leiden sweep. 0.3.1 ranked the label orders again.
  • BatchResult.rescore(verbose=True) prints a line before each label-order ranking.
  • BatchResult.rescore no longer warns about the batch it takes from the label files when metrics= has no batch metric, such as rescore(metrics=["ARI", "NMI"]) on a result with several label files.
  • run_all(batch=...) takes the ids in the cell order of labels_for(dataset) and puts them in each method's cell order. 0.3.1 used the vector as given for every method. A Series or one-column DataFrame indexed by barcode is matched by barcode, in BatchResult.rescore(batch=...) too.
  • BatchResult.rescore(labels=...) aligns a Series or one-column DataFrame indexed by barcode, where 0.3.1 matched it by position. label_order then names the file order chosen.
  • A batch or labels CSV whose first column holds cell ids is aligned by that column. 0.3.1 matched its rows by position. This applies to run_all, rescore and run-all --batch, and to evaluate when the output has cell ids, also for several label files and --column. A column with no cell id is matched by position, with a UserWarning when it holds text. Numbers, such as R's row numbers, are matched by position unless they are exactly the cell ids. A first column with no header whose numbers restart at 0, as pd.concat(...).to_csv(path) writes, is read as an index. The same numbers out of order raise ValueError.
  • For batch=, labels= and these CSVs, ids that are missing, repeated or not cells of the dataset raise ValueError. run_all raises it before any method runs.
  • The first real run fills an existing empty repo_path with the method scripts, where 0.3.1 refused. multibench fetch --scripts does the same. For a repo_path that holds other files but no method scripts, runs raise RuntimeError and scan marks every row not runnable.
  • multibench evaluate also computes the batch metrics when --batch or several --labels are given, as mtb.evaluate does. --task is deprecated. Use --metrics.

docs.title: Scores and figures
docs.text:
• mtb.evaluate clips ASW, iASW, cLISI, ASW_batch, GC and iLISI to 0-1. A value within 1e-12 of 0 or 1 is recorded as 0 or 1.
  • Ranks and fills treat values that agree to 9 decimals as ties.
  • label_order_confidence stays within 0-1, because a runner-up ARI below 0 counts as 0. A value above 1 in an older folder reads 1.0 in summary. The column is numeric, also when every row is blank.
  • mtb.to_long adds the scored_with column. Scores with no record of how they were computed, such as a CSV read back, get unknown and a UserWarning.
  • mtb.plot.bubble draws a column whose rows all hold one value in grey, and every column of a one-method figure. The footnote and a UserWarning name them. Ranks and Overall are unchanged.
  • The chip key of bubble reads ? = a name the package does not know.
  • bubble widens a family pill to fit its header, and a figure of one to three metrics to fit its row labels and key. The height is unchanged.
  • bubble, build_table and bar warn about rows from datasets that share no method, a dataset with only one method, and igraph-scored rows next to stored rows of their dataset when ARI, NMI or iF1 is shown. bar also warns about an incomplete method x dataset table, as bubble does.
  • mtb.recommend warns when modalities or atac names a modality that none of the ranked datasets measured. With long_df=, it also warns when it ranks igraph-scored rows against stored rows of their dataset on ARI, NMI or iF1.
  • mtb.catalog.datasets() no longer has the empty columns assay, tissue, n_cells, n_batches and source.

docs.title: Command line
docs.text:
• multibench plot --input exits with 1 when --dataset or --methods removes all your rows, and warns when it removes some.
  • --format json writes / unescaped.
  • scan and run-all --dry-run add the atac and caveat columns to the short table when they apply.
  • run-all --assume-gpu without --dry-run is a usage error, exit code 2.
  • The dry runs of multibench run and run-all print # Dry run. Nothing was executed. first. run --dry-run then prints its notes, # multibench run would execute: and the command.
  • run-all exits with 3 after saving when a method failed, or a method named in --methods was skipped. 0.3.1 exited with 0. A chain such as run-all ... && plot ... now stops after run-all. A line on stderr names those methods, such as # 1 failed (Seurat_WNN), 1 skipped (totalVI). Other skipped methods go on a # Not run: ... line and do not set 3.
  • The last line of the No method can run error repeats the data path, modalities and other scan options of the call.
Changed messages

Many messages, warnings and printed lines were reworded. Apart from the download error under Downloads, the exception and warning types are the same. A script that matches message text may need an update.

  • Messages printed by multibench name its commands and flags, not Python calls.
  • caveat texts are sentences that start with the method name, such as totalVI needs raw counts. rna.h5 holds non-integer values. The reason column of scan is sentences with their own subjects, such as Environment scmb_r runs only on Linux, not on this computer. or scBridge needs atac_gas.h5, and LUNG has no such file.
  • inputs_for(..., check=True) and the files_reason column of scan say what the method needs and what the folder holds, such as SCALEX (diagonal) needs atac_gas.h5 in <folder>. The folder holds atac_cty.csv, atac_peak.h5, rna.h5 and rna_cty.csv. For MultiMAP and Seurat_v3, the text ends <method> reads both atac_peak.h5 and atac_gas.h5.
  • An unknown method id gets Unknown method stabmap. Did you mean StabMap? mtb.find_methods() shows all methods. A category the method does not run on gets SCALEX does not run on vertical data. Its categories: diagonal. multibench evaluate adds the --name and --labels flags for your own rows.
  • run_all with no method to run raises No method can run on D11 (vertical). With methods=, the message starts None of the requested methods (Matilda, totalVI) can run on D11 (vertical). On macOS and Windows, the error lists only the rows that something else also blocks.
  • The reason for scripts not at MULTIBENCH_SCRIPTS_REF ends with the fix, and scan --strict prints it in full: The method scripts are at 0c68f87, not deadbeef (MULTIBENCH_SCRIPTS_REF). Unset MULTIBENCH_SCRIPTS_REF, or set MULTIBENCH_REPO_PATH to a new folder and run multibench fetch --scripts.
  • A vertical folder whose ATAC file sits under atac_peak.h5 or atac_gas.h5 gets a reason that names the fix, such as MIRA reads atac.h5 for vertical. Rename atac_peak.h5 to atac.h5, or write it with category="vertical". When the file holds the other representation, it reads Matilda needs gene-activity ATAC (atac.h5), and the folder has peaks (atac_peak.h5).
  • The warnings about ATAC feature names give the fix, such as Only 0% of the ATAC feature names look like peaks such as chr1:100-200. If they are peaks, rename them to chr:start-end. They suggest gene activity only when the RNA names are unknown, as in to_canonical, or most ATAC names are RNA gene names.
  • A Series matched by position gets a warning that says how to check its order, such as The labels Series is matched by position, because the embedding has no cell ids. Check that it follows the embedding rows, ... When rescore cannot find the dataset folder, the warning names the folders it looked in and gives the fix, Pass data_path= to mtb.load_batch, or run rescore from the folder where run_all ran. A RUN_OK_NO_LABEL_MATCH record gets the same fix in its note.
  • Count lines say methods when each method has one row, and rows otherwise, such as [scan] 13 of 14 methods have their input files. So does the list header of the run_all error. mtb.run_all(dry_run=True) starts with [run_all] Dry run:. The commands header of run-all --dry-run explains its tags, such as [env missing] marks a row whose environment is not installed.
  • Reworded: the messages of export_dataset, to_canonical, inputs_for, params_for and evaluate. Also the environment messages, file checks, plot and scan warnings, the # Merged with line and the scan, convert and env help. Errors for an unknown modality or metrics= token, a missing folder or table, or a plot --input filter changed too.
  • scan with modalities=["rna", "atac_peak"] no longer warns that scBridge is left out. scBridge reads gene activity.
  • The barcode error for RNA and ATAC with no shared cells points to category="diagonal".
  • labels='obs:cell_type' on a MuData whose column is only in mdata['rna'].obs gets use labels='rna:cell_type'. The .h5mu recipes of multibench layout mosaic and multibench convert --help use --labels rna:cell_type.
  • The raw-count hints follow the selector you passed, such as adt='obsm:protein_counts'.
  • A method that needs a GPU on a computer without one gets <method> needs an NVIDIA GPU, and this computer has none.
  • On macOS and Windows, the refusal of mtb.run starts with Methods run only on Linux and names no install command. That of mtb.env.install starts with Method environments run only on Linux. The summary line of scan says Method environments run only on Linux. and what works on this computer. On Linux, it names mtb.env.doctor() when an environment is missing.
  • A count mismatch in mtb.evaluate names the argument and both counts, such as labels has 60 entries for 90 cells in the embedding. multibench evaluate names the flag and the file.
  • A per-cell CSV with several columns and none chosen gets the columns after the cell ids and how to choose one, such as The --batch file obs_sheet.csv has several columns after the cell ids: celltype, sample. Choose one with --batch-column. A column name that is not in the file gets the same list.
  • Missing batch labels get metrics='all' needs batch labels for ASW_batch, ARI_batch, NMI_batch, GC and iLISI. Pass batch=<vector>, or metrics='clustering'. A batch that no chosen metric uses gets batch= changes nothing here, because metrics=['ARI', 'NMI'] has no batch metric. ...
  • load_results with a result_path that does not exist raises FileNotFoundError naming the path. load_results("mosaic") starts with mosaic has no published tables. and names source='rerun'. multibench plot --category mosaic names --source rerun.
  • The warning of bubble and build_table for several datasets reads This figure averages each method over 3 datasets, D24, D25 and D28. Its rows mix datasets. multibench plot --input with --category prints # Added your 7 rows (MyMethod) to the stored diagonal table, which has 137 rows (source published).
  • bubble on your rows and stored rows under one method name says Your rows and the stored table both have uniPort on D28. Give your rows another name, such as uniPort_rerun, with to_long(method=...). multibench plot names evaluate --name instead.
  • scan and run_all name what does not match, such as Matilda does not run on cross data. Its categories: vertical. or The folder data/MYCITE does not exist. data holds D11, D28 and D52. ... A label file of the wrong length gets cty.csv has 15 labels, but rna.h5 has 20 cells. Give each cell one label, in the order of the cells. ...
  • An unknown method or metric in bubble, build_table, bar and multibench plot gets Unknown method Matlida. Did you mean Matilda? The table has A and B.
  • The warning of export_dataset for gene-activity ATAC with category="mosaic" starts with Every mosaic method reads peak ATAC. and names the fix.
  • mtb.catalog.metrics() describes cLISI and iLISI as the median over cells, scaled to 0-1.
  • The note before the clustering sweep of evaluate names the cell count, the metrics and the Leiden backend, and how to skip the sweep.
  • mtb.io.read_canonical of a missing path names mtb.config.DEFAULT.data_path.
  • mtb.describe_layout(category) prints only that category. The diagonal layout names each method on one line.
  • A failed download of the method scripts names the offline route: copy a fetched scripts folder and set MULTIBENCH_REPO_PATH.
  • env plan, env install and the install warning call an environment without a CPU build a single build, the same archive for CPU and GPU hosts. env status, env doctor and env plan show no flavor= for it.

docs.title: Downloads
docs.text: • mtb.data.fetch and fetch_outputs raise OSError, naming the URL, when a download fails. 0.3.1 raised the urllib error, now kept as __cause__. Code that catches URLError must catch OSError.

docs.title: Removed in 0.3.1
docs.text:
These calls no longer select or report anything and were removed.

Call What happens now find_methods(..., available=...) TypeError: find_methods() got an unexpected keyword argument 'available' method_info(m)["availability"], the "availability" key of mtb.env.plan() rows KeyError. The keys are gone.

docs.title: Deprecated in 0.3.0
docs.text:
Renamed 0.2.1 spellings still work in 0.3.x with a DeprecationWarning and will be removed in 0.4. Removed ones raise an error.

0.2.1 0.3.0 mtb.plan(dataset, category, ...) mtb.scan(dataset, category, ...). Since 0.4 scan has one row per method; the frame with the command column is mtb.run_all(dataset, category, dry_run=True). mtb.plan_commands(...) mtb.scan(...); since 0.4 mtb.run_all(..., dry_run=True) mtb.runtime_hint(m) mtb.method_info(m)["runtime"] mtb.plot.plot_bubble(...) mtb.plot.bubble(...) evaluate(..., task="clustering" / "batch" / "all") evaluate(..., metrics="clustering" / "batch" / "all") evaluate(..., family=...) evaluate(..., metrics=<token>) evaluate(..., only=[...]) evaluate(..., metrics=[...]) load_results(..., method=...) load_results(..., methods=...) load_results(..., metric=[...]) load_results(..., metrics=[...]) load_results(..., task=... / family=...) load_results(..., metrics=<token>) recommend(..., task=... / family=...) recommend(..., metrics=<token>) multibench evaluate --only A,B multibench evaluate --metrics A,B (stderr: warning: --only is deprecated. Use --metrics.)

Passing metrics= together with a deprecated selector raises TypeError: evaluate() got metrics= together with the deprecated ['task']; pass metrics= only.

To find old spellings in your code, run it with python -W error::DeprecationWarning. The warnings then become errors.

These spellings were removed in 0.3.0:

removed error mtb.command_preview(...) AttributeError. Use mtb.run(..., dry_run=True). mtb.io.from_mudata(...) AttributeError. Use mtb.io.export_dataset(mdata, ..., rna="rna", atac="atac", atac_kind="peak", labels="rna:celltype"). mtb.io.write_labels(...) AttributeError. export_dataset writes the label files. By hand, use pd.Series(labels, name="x").to_csv(path, index=False). list_methods(task=...) / (runnable=...) TypeError: list_methods() only takes category since 0.3.0; task=... are find_methods filters - use find_methods(category, task=...) find_methods("vertical", "clustering") (positional filters) TypeError: find_methods() takes from 0 to 1 positional arguments but 2 were given method_info(m, files_dir=...) TypeError: method_info() got an unexpected keyword argument 'files_dir'. The catalog columns are in mtb.catalog.methods(). cite(methods=[...]) TypeError: cite() got an unexpected keyword argument 'methods'. Use cite([...]) or one id per argument. cite([ids], "bibtex") TypeError: cite(): method ids must be strings, got list; pass one list (cite(['Matilda', 'MOFA2'])) or one id per argument. fmt= is keyword-only. inputs_for(dataset, method, category) TypeError: inputs_for argument order is (dataset, category, method) since 0.3.0; you passed (dataset, method, category) labels_for(dataset, method, category) TypeError: labels_for argument order is (dataset, category, method) since 0.3.0; you passed (dataset, method, category) labels_for(dataset, "<data_path>") TypeError: labels_for: pass data_path= by keyword; the 2nd positional argument is category since 0.3.0 (order: (dataset, category, method)) inputs_for(..., ["rna", "adt"]) (positional modalities) TypeError: inputs_for() takes 3 positional arguments but 4 were given scan(dataset, category, data_path) (positional) TypeError: scan() takes from 1 to 2 positional arguments but 3 were given run(method, category, "clustering", ...) (positional task) TypeError: run() takes 2 positional arguments but 3 positional arguments (and 2 keyword-only arguments) were given run_all(dataset, category) without out_dir TypeError: run_all() needs out_dir= for a real run (dry_run=True returns the scan frame without one) BatchResult.rescore(only=...) TypeError: BatchResult.rescore() got an unexpected keyword argument 'only'. Use metrics=. evaluate(output, category, ...) (positional category) TypeError: evaluate() got multiple values for argument 'labels'. labels is the second positional argument, and the rest are keyword-only. evaluate(..., slow_metrics=True) TypeError: evaluate() got slow_metrics=, removed in 0.3.0: pass metrics=[...] without cLISI/iLISI (kBET is computed only when it is named in that list) evaluate(..., column="x") TypeError: evaluate() got column=, removed in 0.3.0: pass the Series/column itself as labels= / batch= / clustering= evaluate(..., metric_set="scib") TypeError: evaluate() got metric_set=, removed in 0.3.0: only the scIB metric set exists - drop the argument to_long(df, method, dataset, category) (positional) TypeError: to_long() takes 1 positional argument but 4 were given to_long(..., needs_labels=True) TypeError: to_long() got an unexpected keyword argument 'needs_labels'. Add the column to the frame. load_results(category, "clustering") (positional) TypeError: load_results() takes from 0 to 1 positional arguments but 2 were given load_results(..., metric_set="scib") TypeError: load_results() got metric_set=, removed in 0.3.0: only the scIB metric set exists - drop the argument available_datasets(..., metric_set=... / clustering=...) TypeError: available_datasets() got an unexpected keyword argument 'metric_set' (likewise 'clustering') mtb.config.category_folder / metric_set_dir, mtb.plot.render / FamilyBlock, mtb.env.group_for and the other mtb.env helpers Still importable, but internal: out of __all__ and hidden from dir().

docs.title: Citation
docs.text: Cite the scMultiBench paper, and the publication of each integration method you run. The paper lists the publication of every method.

docs.title: The paper
docs.text:

  title = {Multitask benchmarking of single-cell multimodal omics integration methods},
  journal = {Nature Methods},
