}

docs.title: Source code
docs.text:
• Benchmark and method scripts: https://github.com/PYangLab/scMultiBench
  • The multibench API, this documentation, the tutorials and the PyPI releases: https://github.com/DSichang/scMultiBench, a fork of the repository above

To cite the software, set version and year to the release you used (multibench.__version__).

software.bib
@software{scmultibench_code,
  author    = {Liu, Chunlei and Ding, Sichang and Yang, Pengyi},
  title     = {{scMultiBench}: a benchmark and Python API for single-cell
               multimodal omics integration},
  url       = {https://github.com/PYangLab/scMultiBench},
  note      = {multibench Python package,
               https://github.com/DSichang/scMultiBench},
  version   = {<multibench.__version__>},
  year      = {2026}
}
Details: reporting a run

Record the package version (multibench.__version__), each method's environment, and the command it ran (the command column of mtb.scan).

run saves one record per method under out_dir. The record holds the environment and its build (cpu, gpu or single), the parameters, the package version, the commit of the method scripts and the computer. The scored_with column of the table mtb.evaluate returns names its Leiden backend, clustering and package version.

The stored results carry the package version that scored them in df.attrs["rerun_version"].

docs.title: Where to look
docs.text:
• Installation and environments: Installation.
  • Running methods and reading metrics: the tutorials for vertical, diagonal, mosaic and cross integration.
  • The full benchmark rankings: the interactive explorer.

docs.title: cLISI / iLISI are NaN on my Mac
docs.text: Install a C++ compiler, then run evaluate again in a new Python session. On macOS, xcode-select --install installs one.

docs.title: mtb.env.install refuses on macOS or Windows
docs.text:
The method environments run only on Linux, so the install refuses here. Installation lists what works on macOS and Windows.

To run on a Linux server, make the commands there: the command column of scan holds the absolute paths of the machine it runs on.

docs.title: Installation
docs.text:
pip install multibench-sc installs the API on Python 3.9 or newer. On macOS and Windows you can use the stored results, check your data with scan, score embeddings and plot. Running a method needs Linux. Windows is not tested.

Summary

conda create -n multibench python=3.11 -y && conda activate multibench
pip install multibench-sc
python -c "import multibench as mtb; print(mtb.__version__)"

docs.title: Step 1: Create an isolated environment
docs.text:
Any fresh Python 3.9+ environment works. Conda is optional: the method environments install without it.

Conda (recommended)Mamba (faster solver)venv terminal
conda create -n multibench python=3.11 -y
conda activate multibench
terminal
mamba create -n multibench python=3.11 -y
mamba activate multibench
terminal
python3.11 -m venv .venv
source .venv/bin/activate

On Windows, activate it with .venv\Scripts\activate.

docs.title: Step 2: Install multibench
docs.text:
terminal
pip install multibench-sc
Dependencies

The install brings numpy, pandas, h5py, anndata, matplotlib, pyyaml, scanpy and scib. PyTorch, R and the method packages are not installed here. Each method's environment holds them.

Developer install

Clone the repository only to edit the notebooks or run the test suite:

terminal
git clone https://github.com/DSichang/scMultiBench.git
cd scMultiBench
pip install -e ".[dev]" --config-settings editable_mode=compat

docs.title: Step 3: Verify the install
docs.text:
terminal
python -c "import multibench as mtb; print(mtb.__version__)"

These calls need no method environment:

import multibench as mtb

print(mtb.find_methods(category="vertical"))

Dataset folder layout shows how to lay out your own dataset.

docs.title: Method environments
docs.text:
Each method runs in its own Linux environment. Install only the ones you need. mtb.env.install downloads prebuilt archives, with no conda needed.

import multibench as mtb

# the environments a category needs: installed or not, with their sizes
mtb.env.install(category="vertical", dry_run=True)
# one method
mtb.env.install(["SCALEX"])
# one category
mtb.env.install(category="vertical")
Details
  • mtb.config.envs_dir is where they go: $MULTIBENCH_ENVS_DIR when set, else the envs directory of the conda or mamba on PATH, else ~/.cache/multibench/envs. print(mtb.config) shows the folder in use.
  • A failed archive download falls back to a build from the lockfile, which needs conda or mamba and takes longer.
  • flavor="cpu" or "gpu" picks the build. By default, a host without an NVIDIA GPU gets the smaller CPU build of the PyTorch environments that have one.
  • The totals of the dry run: categories share environments, so two categories cost less than the sum of their totals. ? disk means the size on disk is not recorded.
  • mtb.env.install skips environments that already exist, so a rerun resumes an interrupted install. With no methods and no category, it installs all 24. Check the total with the dry run first (reference).
Details: method scripts

The first run clones the method scripts from PYangLab/scMultiBench with git. They go to mtb.config.repo_path, which is ~/.cache/multibench/scMultiBench_ref after pip install. The variable MULTIBENCH_SCRIPTS_REF fetches a given commit or tag. On a cluster with offline compute nodes fetches them ahead of time.

On a host without network, clone them on a connected machine with git clone --depth 1 https://github.com/PYangLab/scMultiBench.git <folder> and copy the folder. Then set MULTIBENCH_REPO_PATH to the copy.

docs.title: Google Colab
docs.text:
The tutorials open in Colab from their badge. Choose a GPU runtime first: Runtime -> Change runtime type -> T4 GPU. Each notebook then installs the environments of the methods it runs and runs them, with no conda needed.

Details

On a CPU runtime, an environment that has a smaller CPU build gets that build, and training methods run slower.

The environments each tutorial downloads, with a GPU and without one:

  • vertical RNA + ADT 5.1 GB, 1.1 GB: Matilda and sciPENN
  • vertical RNA + ATAC 1.8 GB, 1.2 GB: scMM and VIMCCA
  • vertical RNA + ADT + ATAC 4.0 GB, 1.5 GB: Matilda and UINMF
  • diagonal [RNA, ATAC] 0.9 GB: iNMF and online_iNMF
  • diagonal [multiple RNA, multiple ATAC] 0.9 GB: iNMF and online_iNMF
  • mosaic [RNA, RNA + ADT, ADT] 5.4 GB, 1.8 GB: StabMap and scMoMaT
  • mosaic [RNA, RNA + ATAC, ATAC] 5.4 GB, 1.8 GB: StabMap and scMoMaT
  • mosaic Mixed, with shared modality 0.9 GB: StabMap and UINMF
  • mosaic Mixed, without shared modality 5.4 GB, 1.8 GB: StabMap and scMoMaT
  • cross Multiple RNA + ADT 3.0 GB, 1.4 GB: StabMap and sciPENN
  • cross Multiple RNA + ATAC 2.0 GB, 1.4 GB: StabMap and scMM
  • cross Multiple ADT + ATAC 0.9 GB: StabMap and UINMF
  • cross Multiple RNA + ADT + ATAC 0.9 GB: StabMap and UINMF
  • end-to-end 3.0 GB, 0.6 GB: Matilda

Every task has more methods than its tutorial runs. The last section of each tutorial links a notebook that runs them all. Those download more, up to 38.2 GB for vertical RNA + ATAC on a GPU runtime; each notebook states its size.

docs.title: Get the data
docs.text:
Each tutorial downloads its dataset on first run. Datasets go to mtb.config.data_path: ~/.cache/multibench/data after pip install, <repo>/data in a developer install.

import multibench as mtb

mtb.catalog.datasets().dataset.tolist()   # ['D11', 'D28', 'D45', 'D46', 'D52', 'D22mini', ...]
mtb.data.fetch("D11")                     # no-op when already present
Details

The tutorials run on one dataset per integration task. D11 is a benchmark dataset; each mini is a smaller copy of one, with a subset of its cells, genes and peaks:

Task Dataset Size vertical, RNA + ADT D11 11 MB vertical, RNA + ATAC D27mini_vertical 24 MB vertical, RNA + ADT + ATAC D22mini 8 MB diagonal, [RNA, ATAC] D27mini 15 MB diagonal, [multiple RNA, multiple ATAC] D37mini 12 MB mosaic, [RNA, RNA + ADT, ADT] D38mini 2 MB mosaic, [RNA, RNA + ATAC, ATAC] D45mini 11 MB mosaic, Mixed, with shared modality D46mini 4 MB mosaic, Mixed, without shared modality D49mini 5 MB cross, Multiple RNA + ADT D52mini 2 MB cross, Multiple RNA + ATAC D56mini 10 MB cross, Multiple ADT + ATAC D58mini 7 MB cross, Multiple RNA + ADT + ATAC D59mini 8 MB

The benchmark datasets D28 (diagonal, 137 MB), D45 (mosaic, 290 MB), D46 (mosaic, 97 MB) and D52 (cross, 179 MB) are also fetchable.

MULTIBENCH_DATA_PATH sets the data path. Without it, and with XDG_CACHE_HOME set, the data path after pip install is $XDG_CACHE_HOME/multibench/data. print(mtb.config) shows the path in use.

To download a dataset by hand, for example D11:

terminal
DATA=~/.cache/multibench/data   # the data_path that print(mtb.config) shows
URL=https://github.com/DSichang/scMultiBench/releases/download/data-v1
mkdir -p "$DATA"
wget -qO- "$URL/D11.tar.gz" | tar xz -C "$DATA"

The full collection of processed datasets is linked from the scMultiBench README. Unpack a dataset under the data path, or anywhere else and pass its folder path as dataset.

docs.title: On a cluster with offline compute nodes
docs.text:
Prepare everything on a login node with network. The compute nodes then need no download. Keep the folders below on storage that the compute nodes can read.

login node
python3 -m venv /shared/multibench/venv
source /shared/multibench/venv/bin/activate
pip install "multibench-sc>=0.4.0"
export MULTIBENCH_ENVS_DIR=/shared/multibench/envs
export MULTIBENCH_DATA_PATH=/shared/multibench/data
export MULTIBENCH_REPO_PATH=/shared/multibench/scripts
# the method scripts, so the compute nodes need no download
git clone --depth 1 https://github.com/PYangLab/scMultiBench.git "$MULTIBENCH_REPO_PATH"
python prepare.py
prepare.py
import multibench as mtb

# flavor="gpu": for jobs on GPU nodes
mtb.env.install(["StabMap", "scMoMaT"], flavor="gpu")
# optional: a demo mosaic dataset to test the setup
mtb.data.fetch("D45mini")
# LAB: your dataset folder under $MULTIBENCH_DATA_PATH
# assume_gpu=True: check GPU-only methods for the GPU nodes, not this node
print(mtb.scan("LAB", "mosaic", methods=["StabMap", "scMoMaT"], assume_gpu=True))

Submit one job per method, each with its own out_dir. Request a GPU only for a method that uses one. mtb.method_info("M") shows whether a method uses a GPU.

run_one.py
import sys
import multibench as mtb

m = sys.argv[1]
res = mtb.run("LAB", "mosaic", methods=[m], out_dir=f"runs/{m}", timeout=14400)
# a failed or timed-out method ends the script with an error, so Slurm marks the job failed
bad = res.summary[res.summary.status.isin(["failed", "timeout"])]
assert bad.empty, bad
job.sh (Slurm)
#!/bin/bash
#SBATCH --time=05:00:00
source /shared/multibench/venv/bin/activate
export MULTIBENCH_ENVS_DIR=/shared/multibench/envs
export MULTIBENCH_DATA_PATH=/shared/multibench/data
export MULTIBENCH_REPO_PATH=/shared/multibench/scripts
python run_one.py "$1"
login node
# StabMap does not use a GPU; scMoMaT uses one when present
sbatch job.sh StabMap
sbatch --gres=gpu:1 job.sh scMoMaT

When the jobs have finished, plot them together:

import pandas as pd
import multibench as mtb

long = pd.concat([mtb.load_run(f"runs/{m}").long for m in ["StabMap", "scMoMaT"]])
mtb.plot.bubble(long, save="lab.pdf")
Details

The dry run of mtb.env.install gives the download sizes. An unpacked environment is larger. Check it with du after the first install.

Each input file is read as a dense matrix. Request at least features x cells x 8 bytes of memory per input file.

The runtimes in mtb.method_info("M") were observed on a GPU host. For a method that uses a GPU, allow several times longer on a CPU node.

docs.title: Upgrading
docs.text: 0.4 renamed or removed some names of 0.3, and removed the command line. Changes lists each one.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text:
OSError: Environment <env> of <method> is not installed

The method's environment is missing. Run the install command the message names, for example mtb.env.install(["<method>"]). mtb.scan() names it per method.

Environment <env> was not installed by this version of multibench

A conda environment has the name of a method's environment, but this version of multibench did not install it, so it is not used: an environment you made yourself, or one that multibench 0.3.9 or older built from a recipe, or 0.3.0 or older unpacked from an archive. Rename or remove the folder the message names, then run mtb.env.install(["<method>"]).

LinuxOnlyError: Methods run only on Linux ...

Methods cannot run on macOS or Windows. Run the call on a Linux machine. mtb.scan shows each method's command on this computer. The error is an OSError and a RuntimeError; mtb.env.install raises it too.

FileNotFoundError: ... 'conda' from a run

No method environment is installed yet and this host has no conda. Install the method's environment with mtb.env.install(["<method>"]).

OSError naming envs_dir, with MULTIBENCH_RUN_MODE=prefix

Prefix mode is forced, but the environment is not under envs_dir. Install it (mtb.env.install(["<method>"])), point MULTIBENCH_ENVS_DIR at the folder that holds it, or unset MULTIBENCH_RUN_MODE.

RuntimeError: Conda is not installed on this computer. Environment <env> has a packed archive.

Only a lockfile build needs conda. Leave out build=True.

ImportError: No module named scib from mtb.evaluate

multibench was installed with --no-deps or into another interpreter. Run pip install multibench-sc in the environment you import from.

cLISI / iLISI are NaN, with a warning naming knn_graph.o

Both need scib's compiled LISI helper, which ships as a Linux x86-64 binary. On other platforms evaluate() rebuilds it automatically when a C++ compiler (g++, c++ or clang++) is on PATH.

Without a compiler, install one (Xcode command-line tools on macOS) and rerun evaluate in a new Python session, or run the g++ command the warning prints. The other metrics are computed either way.

unsupported input format

mtb.io.export_dataset takes an in-memory AnnData or MuData. Read other formats into an AnnData first.

If the problem remains, open an issue with the output of python -c "import multibench as mtb; print(mtb.__version__)" and pip freeze.

Next: the Quickstart, or run a method with the Run a method tutorial.

docs.title: How scMultiBench works
docs.text: scMultiBench is a benchmark of single-cell multimodal integration methods. The multibench package is its Python API.

docs.title: What scMultiBench covers
docs.text:
The benchmark groups datasets into four scenarios by how the data were measured. Each scenario is a category value in the API:

  • Vertical: several modalities measured in the same cells, for example CITE-seq or 10x Multiome.
  • Diagonal: modalities measured in different cells, for example scRNA-seq and scATAC-seq from separate experiments.
  • Mosaic: several batches, only some sharing a modality, joined by a paired batch.
  • Cross: several batches, each with every modality, for example one CITE-seq assay from several donors.
Details

The benchmark evaluates dimension reduction, batch correction, clustering and classification.

Its datasets are real and simulated, and cover RNA, ADT and ATAC.

docs.title: How it evaluates
docs.text:
Each task has its own metric panel. The scores are combined into per-method rank scores. For the full ranking per scenario, see the paper's decision tree (Fig. 6) or the interactive explorer.

Details

The metric panels are:

  • Dimension reduction, batch correction and clustering: scIB metrics such as kBET, iLISI, ASW, graph connectivity, ARI and NMI.
  • Classification: OCA, ACA, Spec, Sens and F1.
  • Every task: runtime and peak memory.

In the package, mtb.evaluate computes the scIB metrics and the classification metrics for an embedding.

docs.title: Next steps
docs.text:
• Install: pip install multibench-sc, then import multibench. See Installation.
  • First run: Quickstart.
  • Tutorials: vertical, diagonal, mosaic, cross, and the end-to-end walkthrough.
  • Explore: interactive Shiny explorer.
  • API: multibench.

docs.title: Quickstart
docs.text:
Five steps take you from finding methods to plotting your run next to the stored results. Only step 3 runs a method. It needs Linux and a method environment. The other steps also work on macOS and Windows.

  • CITE-seq: see Your own data below.
  • 10x Multiome, unpaired RNA + ATAC or one file per batch: see Your own data as a dataset folder.
Words used on this site embedding A table with one row per cell and tens to hundreds of numbers per cell, like adata.obsm["X_pca"]. category How your cells were measured, for example vertical for CITE-seq from one experiment. variant One version of a method for one data type, such as RNA + ADT. role The name of one input file, such as rna or adt. dataset folder One folder that holds the input files of a dataset, such as rna.h5 and cty.csv. raw counts Integer counts per cell and feature, before any normalization. demo dataset A benchmark dataset that mtb.data.fetch downloads, such as D11 or D28. stored results The scores that ship with the package: its own runs of the methods, one dataset per category. long table A table with one row per method, dataset and metric. cell order The order of the rows in a method's output. For diagonal data most methods put the RNA cells first, then the ATAC cells. run writes each cell's barcode into embedding.h5, and evaluate(dataset=) matches the label files by them.

Summary

import multibench as mtb, pandas as pd

# 1. methods for unpaired RNA + ATAC (diagonal)
mtb.find_methods(category="diagonal", modalities=["rna", "atac"])

# 2. plot the stored results of dataset D28
df = mtb.load_results("diagonal", dataset="D28")
mtb.plot.bubble(df, metrics=["ARI", "NMI", "cLISI"], save="fig.pdf")

# 3. run and score a method on D28 (Linux only)
mtb.data.fetch("D28")
mtb.env.install(["SCALEX"])
res = mtb.run("D28", "diagonal", methods=["SCALEX"], out_dir="out/")

# 4. score an embedding of your own (adata: your AnnData)
scores = mtb.evaluate(adata, labels="celltype", obsm="X_pca", method="PCA")

# 5. plot your run of step 3 next to the stored results (Linux only)
mine = res.long.assign(method=res.long.method + " (this run)")
mtb.plot.bubble(pd.concat([df, mine]), metrics=["ARI", "NMI", "cLISI"])

docs.title: Step 1: Discover methods for your data
docs.text:
Pick the category that matches how your data was measured, then filter by modality:

  • vertical: several modalities measured in the same cells
  • diagonal: modalities measured in different cells
  • mosaic: several batches, only some sharing a modality
  • cross: several batches, each with every modality (RNA+ADT here)

For several samples or donors:

  • 10x Multiome samples: use vertical. Keep all cells in one folder and pass each cell's sample as batch= to run or evaluate.
  • CITE-seq donors: use vertical in the same way. It takes any number of donors. For run, batch= takes the donor column itself, such as batch=adata.obs["donor"], not its name. The cross category integrates the donors as batches and reads a fixed number of them, three for RNA + ADT: see the One file per batch tab. With another number of donors, use vertical, as in the recipe Another number of donors.
import multibench as mtb

mtb.find_methods(category="diagonal", modalities=["rna", "atac"])
# -> ['SCALEX', 'Seurat_v5', 'scBridge', 'VIPCCA', 'Portal', 'uniPort',
#     'sciCAN', 'scJoint', 'GLUE', 'MultiMAP', 'iNMF', 'online_iNMF', 'Conos',
#     'Seurat_v3']

Each method reads ATAC either as peaks or as gene-activity scores. With a peak matrix only, keep the methods that read peaks:

mtb.find_methods(category="diagonal", modalities=["atac_peak"])
# -> ['Seurat_v5', 'GLUE', 'MultiMAP', 'Seurat_v3']

MultiMAP and Seurat_v3 also need gene activity. Seurat_v5 needs RNA and ATAC from the same cells. See My ATAC is peaks only.

Inspect a candidate, or rank candidates from the stored results:

info = mtb.method_info("SCALEX")
info["env"], info["atac"], info["needs_labels"], info["reference"]["doi"]
# ('scmb_torch', 'gene_activity', False, '10.1038/s41467-022-33758-z')
info["runtime"]    # {..., 'tier': 'slow', 'worst_sec': 2233, ...}
mtb.recommend("diagonal", modalities=["rna", "atac"])
Details

find_methods also filters by needs_labels, and every filter must hold. mtb.recommend("diagonal", methods=mtb.find_methods("diagonal", needs_labels=False)) ranks the methods that run without labels.

recommend lists methods without stored results last, with grand_score NaN. recommend(..., metrics="batch") ranks on the batch-correction metrics instead.

For CITE-seq donors, the vertical category has 14 RNA + ADT methods and stored results on D11. The cross category has 10 RNA + ADT methods, which integrate the donors as batches, and stored results on D52. These methods read batches 1-3.

docs.title: Step 2: Plot the stored results
docs.text:
Load the stored results of a dataset and draw the article's bubble table. load_results returns a long table: one row per method, dataset and metric.

df = mtb.load_results("diagonal", dataset="D28")
fig = mtb.plot.bubble(df, metrics=["ARI", "NMI", "cLISI"], save="fig.pdf")
Details

The stored results are the package's own runs of the methods, one dataset per category: D11, D28, D45 and D52. mtb.catalog.datasets() marks them has_results.

load_results also takes methods and metrics (reference). mtb.recommend("diagonal", long_df=df, metrics=["ARI", "NMI", "cLISI"]) gives the numbers behind the figure, in its row order.

docs.title: Step 3: Run a method
docs.text:
mtb.run runs the methods you name on a dataset folder, each in its own environment, and scores each output. Install the method's environment first, on Linux. mtb.env.install(..., dry_run=True) shows the download first.

mtb.data.fetch("D28")  # 137 MB, downloaded once
mtb.env.install(["SCALEX"])
res = mtb.run("D28", "diagonal", methods=["SCALEX"], out_dir="out/")
res.summary      # status, run time and every score
Details

The reason column of res.summary says why a method failed or was skipped. mtb.scan("D28", "diagonal", methods=["SCALEX"]) runs nothing and returns the plan: per method, whether it can run here, why not, and the command run would execute. It works on any platform.

mtb.load_run("out/") reloads the result later, and res.embedding("SCALEX") returns the embedding as an AnnData: obs holds each cell's label, and its batch when the run had several batches.

docs.title: Your own data
docs.text:
Give raw counts. On macOS and Windows you can prepare the folder, check it, preview the commands, score your own embedding and plot. Running a method needs Linux.

CITE-seq on a laptopLinux, environments installed 
import anndata as ad
import multibench as mtb
import pandas as pd
import scanpy as sc

# adata: RNA counts in X, ADT counts in obsm["protein"], cell types in obs
adata = ad.read_h5ad("my_citeseq.h5ad")
mtb.io.export_dataset(adata, "data/MYCITE", rna="X", adt="obsm:protein",
                      labels="obs:celltype")
mtb.scan("data/MYCITE", "vertical")

# compare two PCA embeddings: RNA and ADT
pc = adata.copy()
sc.pp.normalize_total(pc)
sc.pp.log1p(pc)
sc.pp.highly_variable_genes(pc, n_top_genes=2000)
sc.pp.pca(pc)
adata.obsm["X_pca"] = pc.obsm["X_pca"]
adt = sc.AnnData(adata.obsm["protein"])
sc.pp.normalize_total(adt)
sc.pp.log1p(adt)
sc.pp.pca(adt, n_comps=min(20, adt.n_vars - 1))
adata.obsm["X_adt"] = adt.obsm["X_pca"]
mine = pd.concat([
    mtb.evaluate(adata, labels="celltype", obsm="X_pca", method="RNA PCA",
                 dataset="MYCITE", category="vertical"),
    mtb.evaluate(adata, labels="celltype", obsm="X_adt", method="ADT PCA",
                 dataset="MYCITE", category="vertical"),
])
print(mine.pivot(index="method", columns="metric", values="value").round(2))
mtb.plot.bubble(mine)

With two rows, the darker one is the better of the two in each column. The printed table shows how far apart they are.

When the RNA counts are in a layer, such as adata.layers["counts"], change two lines: pass rna="layer:counts" to export_dataset, and start the PCA from the counts with pc = sc.AnnData(adata.layers["counts"].copy()).

import anndata as ad
import multibench as mtb

adata = ad.read_h5ad("my_citeseq.h5ad")
mtb.io.export_dataset(adata, "data/MYCITE", rna="X", adt="obsm:protein",
                      labels="obs:celltype")
mtb.scan("data/MYCITE", "vertical")
res = mtb.run("data/MYCITE", "vertical", out_dir="out/")
res.summary
res.plot()

run runs every method that scan marks runnable, scores each output and saves the results under out_dir.

With several donors or samples in the file, add batch=adata.obs["donor"] to run. The summary then has the batch metrics. The recipe Another number of donors has the steps.

10x Multiome, unpaired RNA + ATAC and one file per batch have their own recipes in Your own data as a dataset folder. Dataset folder layout lists the file names each category expects.

docs.title: Step 4: Score an embedding of your own
docs.text:
mtb.evaluate scores any embedding with the article's metrics against cell-type labels, and returns the long table. run calls it for you. Call it yourself for an embedding made outside the package, such as a PCA:

scores = mtb.evaluate(adata, labels="celltype", obsm="X_pca", method="PCA")
# columns: metric, value, method, dataset, category, source, scored_with
Details

metrics=None, the default, computes every metric that applies except kBET. That is the clustering family, plus the batch family when there is a batch vector or several label files, plus classification for two or more batches outside vertical. See the metrics= vocabulary.

The Leiden clusters behind ARI, NMI, ASW, iASW and iF1 are searched to the number of cell types, and those behind ARI_batch and NMI_batch to the number of batches. A metrics= list without these skips the search.

For an output of a dataset folder, pass dataset=, category= and method= instead of labels: the label files are matched to the cells by the barcodes run writes into embedding.h5.

docs.title: Step 5: Plot your run with the stored results
docs.text:
res.long holds the scores of your run as a long table. Plot it with the stored results of D28, each method under a name the table does not have yet.

The stored results cover one dataset per category. Rows from your own dataset go in a figure of their own.

import pandas as pd

mine = res.long.assign(method=res.long.method + " (this run)")
combined = pd.concat([df, mine], ignore_index=True)
mtb.plot.bubble(combined, metrics=["ARI", "NMI", "cLISI"], save="compare.pdf")
Details

A new run's scores differ a little from the stored ones. See Are my numbers comparable?

For an embedding of your own, mtb.evaluate(..., method="Mine", dataset="D28", category="diagonal") gives the same long table. Add your own method shows how.

  • Vertical / diagonal / mosaic / cross: one notebook per integration task, on a small dataset and on your own data. These are the first of each category.
  • Run a method: any of the 36 methods, on a dataset folder.

docs.title: Interactive explorer (Shiny)
docs.text:
The Shiny explorer is a hosted dashboard. It shows the full benchmark results for every method and dataset, without writing code.

Open the Shiny explorer ↗

docs.title: What you can explore
docs.text:
• scIB metrics

    Batch-correction and bio-conservation scores per method, as bubble tables and overall rankings.

  • Integration

    Embeddings, side by side, for each integration scenario.

  • Time and memory

    Runtime and peak memory per method.

docs.title: In Python
docs.text: mtb.load_results reads the stored results that ship with the package. They cover one dataset per category. mtb.plot.bubble draws them, as Load and plot results shows.

docs.title: Catalog (mtb.catalog)
docs.text:
The datasets and the metrics, as DataFrames.

Name Summary mtb.catalog.datasets The datasets mtb.data.fetch downloads or mtb.load_results holds. mtb.catalog.metrics Table describing the metrics: one row per metric code.

docs.title: mtb.catalog.datasets
docs.text:
datasets(*, category: str | None = None) -> DataFrame

The datasets mtb.data.fetch downloads or mtb.load_results holds.

PARAMETERS DESCRIPTION category

vertical, diagonal, mosaic or cross: only the datasets of that category; None = all.

type str | None default None

RETURNS DESCRIPTION DataFrame

One row per dataset: dataset, category and has_results (mtb.load_results has stored results for it). mtb.data.fetch downloads every one.

Examples

>>> import multibench as mtb
>>> ds = mtb.catalog.datasets()
>>> ds.dataset.tolist()
>>> ds[ds.has_results]

docs.title: mtb.catalog.metrics
docs.text:
metrics() -> DataFrame

Table describing the metrics: one row per metric code.

RETURNS DESCRIPTION DataFrame

One row per metric code: metric, family (clustering, batch or classification, the families metrics= takes) and description.

Examples

>>> import multibench as mtb
>>> tab = mtb.catalog.metrics()
>>> tab.set_index("metric").loc["kBET", "description"]
See Also

mtb.evaluate : computes these metrics for an embedding.

docs.title: Compare
docs.text:
Read the stored results, the package's own runs of its methods, and rank the methods of a category. Are my numbers comparable? says what to expect when you add your own runs.

Name Summary mtb.load_results Load the stored results as one long table. mtb.recommend The overall score and row order of mtb.plot.bubble, best first.

docs.title: mtb.load_results
docs.text:
load_results(
    category: str | None = None,
    *,
    dataset: str | list[str] | None = None,
    methods: str | list[str] | None = None,
    metrics=None,
) -> DataFrame

Load the stored results as one long table.

The stored results are the package's own runs of its methods on the benchmark datasets, scored with mtb.evaluate. The table concatenates with the long table mtb.evaluate returns.

PARAMETERS DESCRIPTION category

Integration category (vertical, diagonal, mosaic or cross); None = every category.

type str default None

dataset

Dataset id(s), e.g. "D11" or ["D11", "D28"]; None = every dataset of the category. mtb.catalog.datasets() lists them.

type str or list of str default None

methods

Method(s) to keep, in any case or spelling ("mofa+" -> MOFA2); None = every method.

type str or list of str default None

metrics

None / "all" = every metric; or "clustering", "batch", "classification", or a list of codes such as ["ARI", "NMI"].

type None, str or list of str default None

RETURNS DESCRIPTION DataFrame

One row per score: metric, value, method, dataset, category, source, scored_with. attrs["rerun_version"] holds the package version that scored the stored rows.

RAISES DESCRIPTION FileNotFoundError

No stored results for a requested category or dataset; the message names the datasets there are.

KeyError

Unknown method name in methods, with a did-you-mean hint.

ValueError

Unknown category or metrics.

WARNS DESCRIPTION UserWarning

The selection leaves no rows, for example metrics="classification": the stored results have none.

Examples

>>> import multibench as mtb
>>> long = mtb.load_results("vertical", dataset="D11")
>>> mtb.load_results("diagonal", dataset="D28", metrics="clustering")
See Also

mtb.evaluate : scores your own embedding into this shape. mtb.plot.bubble : draws the table.

docs.title: mtb.recommend
docs.text:
recommend(
    category: str,
    *,
    modalities: list[str] | None = None,
    methods: list[str] | None = None,
    metrics=None,
    long_df: DataFrame | None = None,
) -> DataFrame

The overall score and row order of mtb.plot.bubble, best first.

Within each dataset the methods are ranked on each metric; each per-dataset score is the mean rank over the metrics, min-max scaled so that the best stored method scores 1 and the worst 0, and grand_score is the mean over the datasets. Your rows are ranked against the stored rows, so these keep their scores and order. Without long_df=, the methods the package runs for the category without stored results are listed last.

PARAMETERS DESCRIPTION category

Integration category: vertical, diagonal, mosaic or cross.

type str

modalities

Keep only methods that read all of these modalities, e.g. ["rna", "adt"], as in mtb.find_methods; None = no filter.

type list of str default None

methods

Rank only these methods, among themselves; None = every method.

type list of str default None

metrics

None = every metric present, as mtb.plot.bubble; or a family, a code, or a list of codes and families.

type None, str or list of str default None

long_df

A long table to rank instead of the stored results, such as pd.concat([mtb.load_results(category), mine]).

type DataFrame default None

RETURNS DESCRIPTION DataFrame

One row per method, best first: method, grand_score, needs_labels, runtime_tier, worst_sec and env.

RAISES DESCRIPTION ValueError

Nothing left to rank, long_df repeating stored method/dataset rows, your rows on another dataset than the stored rows, or modalities naming data that none of the ranked datasets measured (pass such scores as long_df=).

KeyError

Unknown method name in methods, with a did-you-mean hint.

WARNS DESCRIPTION UserWarning

One message: partial coverage, methods left out and why.

Examples

>>> import multibench as mtb
>>> mtb.recommend("vertical", modalities=["rna", "adt"])
>>> free = mtb.find_methods("vertical", needs_labels=False)
>>> mtb.recommend("vertical", methods=free)
>>> both = pd.concat([mtb.load_results("vertical"), mine])
>>> mtb.recommend("vertical", long_df=both)

docs.title: Configuration (mtb.config)
docs.text:
The paths and settings every function reads. mtb.config holds them: set one, such as mtb.config.data_path = "/scratch/data", to use your own data folder, environment folder or Leiden backend.

Name Summary mtb.config The paths and settings every multibench function reads.

docs.title: Environment variables
docs.text:
variable effect MULTIBENCH_DATA_PATH The folder that holds the dataset folders (data_path). MULTIBENCH_ENVS_DIR Where method environments are installed and looked up (envs_dir). MULTIBENCH_REPO_PATH Where the method scripts are, or are downloaded to on first use (repo_path). MULTIBENCH_SCRIPTS_REF A commit or tag of the method scripts to download instead of the default branch. MULTIBENCH_RUN_MODE prefix or conda: how a run enters an environment. How the environment is entered describes both.

A value assigned in Python wins over the variable. print(mtb.config) prints each setting.

docs.title: mtb.config
docs.text:
Settings

The paths and settings every multibench function reads.

mtb.config is one of these: set a field to change it, for example mtb.config.data_path = "/scratch/data", or set MULTIBENCH_DATA_PATH, MULTIBENCH_REPO_PATH and MULTIBENCH_ENVS_DIR in the shell. A value assigned in Python wins over the variable; None goes back to the default. print(mtb.config) shows every field; a misspelt field raises AttributeError.

ATTRIBUTES DESCRIPTION data_path

Data root that holds the dataset folders; mtb.data.fetch, mtb.scan and mtb.run use it. Default $MULTIBENCH_DATA_PATH, else <base>/data.

type Path

repo_path

Folder of the method scripts (tools_scripts/), fetched there on the first run when absent or empty. Default $MULTIBENCH_REPO_PATH, else <base>/scMultiBench_ref.

type Path

envs_dir

Where the method environments live (<envs_dir>/<env>). Default $MULTIBENCH_ENVS_DIR, else the first writable envs folder of the conda on PATH, else ~/.cache/multibench/envs.

type Path

leiden_flavor

Leiden backend of the clustering in mtb.evaluate: "leidenalg" (default, the article's and the stored results') or "igraph" (faster).

type str

Examples

>>> import multibench as mtb
>>> mtb.config.data_path = "/scratch/data"
>>> # before mtb.env.install(...)
>>> mtb.config.envs_dir = "/scratch/envs"
>>> print(mtb.config)
See Also

mtb.env.install : installs the method envs under envs_dir. mtb.data.fetch : downloads demo datasets into data_path.

docs.title: Datasets (mtb.data)
docs.text:
Download the demo datasets the tutorials use into mtb.config.data_path. mtb.catalog.datasets() lists them. mtb.data.write_example writes the example files that the own-data section of each tutorial reads.

Name Summary mtb.data.fetch Download demo datasets into the data root, skipping those present. mtb.data.write_example Write the example files of a tutorial dataset as .h5ad files.

docs.title: mtb.data.fetch
docs.text:
fetch(*datasets: str, verbose: bool = True) -> 'Path | list[Path]'

Download demo datasets into the data root, skipping those present.

PARAMETERS DESCRIPTION *datasets

Dataset ids; mtb.catalog.datasets() lists them.

type str default ()

verbose

Print one "downloading ..." line per dataset.

type bool default True

RETURNS DESCRIPTION pathlib.Path or list of pathlib.Path

The dataset folder, <data root>/<dataset>/; a list of them for several datasets.

RAISES DESCRIPTION ValueError

A dataset id that cannot be downloaded (the message lists the ids).

OSError

The download failed; the message names the URL.

Examples

>>> import multibench as mtb
>>> folder = mtb.data.fetch("D11")          # about 11 MB
>>> mtb.scan(folder, "vertical")
Notes

A non-empty <data root>/<dataset>/ counts as present and is left alone. Each archive is unpacked into a temporary folder under the data root and then moved into place.

docs.title: mtb.data.write_example
docs.text:
write_example(
    dataset: str, folder: Path | str = ".", *, verbose: bool = True
) -> None

Write the example files of a tutorial dataset as .h5ad files.

The files hold a part of the dataset in the shape that your own data usually has: one .h5ad file per object, with the cell types in obs["celltype"]. The own-data section of each tutorial reads them until you put your own files in their place. They are named my_*.h5ad; the printed lines say what each holds. A file of your own with such a name is kept.

PARAMETERS DESCRIPTION dataset

Id of a tutorial dataset, such as "D11". It has to be in the data root: mtb.data.fetch(dataset) downloads it.

type str

folder

Folder the files are written to; it is created when it does not exist. The default is the current folder.

type Path | str default '.'

verbose

Print one line per file.

type bool default True

RAISES DESCRIPTION ValueError

No example is defined for dataset (the message lists the ids).

FileNotFoundError

The dataset is not in the data root; the message gives the fetch call.

Examples

>>> import multibench as mtb
>>> mtb.data.fetch("D11")
>>> mtb.data.write_example("D11")       # my_file.h5ad: RNA in X, ADT in obsm
See Also

mtb.data.fetch : download the dataset that the example is made from. mtb.io.export_dataset : write the objects read from the files as a dataset folder.

docs.title: Discover
docs.text:
Find methods and see what each one needs. Every call works offline.

Name Summary mtb.find_methods Return the method ids that match every filter you pass. mtb.method_info Return everything known about one method as a flat dict. mtb.params_for Return the hyperparameters of one method variant.

docs.title: mtb.find_methods
docs.text:
find_methods(
    category: str | None = None,
    *,
    modalities: list[str] | set[str] | None = None,
    needs_labels: bool | None = None,
) -> list[str]

Return the method ids that match every filter you pass.

A method matches when one of its variants meets category, modalities and needs_labels together.

PARAMETERS DESCRIPTION category

Integration category: vertical, diagonal, mosaic or cross; None = any.

type str | None default None

modalities

Modalities a variant must consume, e.g. ["rna", "adt"]; "atac_peak" / "atac_gas" also select by ATAC representation. None = no filter.

type list[str] | set[str] | None default None

needs_labels

True = a matching variant needs cell-type labels; False = one runs without them; None = no filter.

type bool | None default None

RETURNS DESCRIPTION list[str]

Method ids in the package's order.

RAISES DESCRIPTION ValueError

Unknown category or modality token.

TypeError

modalities is a bare string, not a list.

Examples

>>> import multibench as mtb
>>> mtb.find_methods("vertical", modalities=["rna", "adt"])
>>> mtb.find_methods("vertical", modalities=["rna", "adt"], needs_labels=False)
See Also

mtb.method_info : the per-variant supports table these filters are read from. mtb.scan : which of these methods can actually run on a given dataset.

docs.title: mtb.method_info
docs.text:
method_info(method: str) -> dict

Return everything known about one method as a flat dict.

PARAMETERS DESCRIPTION method

Method id, e.g. "Matilda"; see mtb.find_methods().

type str

RETURNS DESCRIPTION dict

One flat record:

id, language, notes     the method id, 'python' or 'R', a summary
categories              the integration categories it runs in
env                     the conda env run executes it in
atac                    'peak' / 'gene_activity' / None
needs_labels            any variant reads cell-type labels
supports                one entry per variant: category, modalities,
                        output_kind, needs_labels, labels,
                        reference_batch
runtime                 tier, worst_sec, observed, host, note
gpu                     'required' / 'used when present' / 'not used'
cpu_params              the flags that turn CUDA off on a CPU host
setup_hint              a step to take before the first run, or ''
repo_url                the upstream code the benchmark ran
reference               {doi, title, authors, journal, year}
RAISES DESCRIPTION KeyError

Unknown method id. The message suggests a close match.

Examples

>>> import multibench as mtb
>>> info = mtb.method_info("Matilda")
>>> # one entry per variant: category, modalities, labels ...
>>> info["supports"]
See Also

mtb.params_for : the hyperparameters of one variant, with upstream defaults. mtb.find_methods : filter methods by category, modalities, labels, ATAC representation.

docs.title: mtb.params_for
docs.text:
params_for(
    method: str,
    category: str | None = None,
    modalities: list[str] | set[str] | None = None,
) -> dict

Return the hyperparameters of one method variant.

Call it before run(params=...) to see what a method accepts and what it runs with when you pass nothing.

PARAMETERS DESCRIPTION method

Method id, e.g. "Matilda"; see mtb.find_methods().

type str

category

Integration category of the variant: vertical, diagonal, mosaic or cross; None = infer it from the other arguments.

type str | None default None

modalities

Modality tokens of the variant, e.g. ["rna", "adt"]; None = infer it from the other arguments.

type list[str] | set[str] | None default None

RETURNS DESCRIPTION dict

method, variant ('category:mods', or several that take the same parameters), tunable (what params= can set, {name: {"type", "default"}}; default is what a run uses when you pass nothing), fixed_in_script (what the script pins, with file:line), upstream_knobs (what its library documents but the script does not expose) and upstream_url.

RAISES DESCRIPTION KeyError

Unknown method, a declared stub, or no variant for category / modalities.

ValueError

Unknown category or modality token, or several variants with other parameters fit (the message spells out the call that selects one).

Examples

>>> import multibench as mtb
>>> p = mtb.params_for("Matilda", "vertical", ["rna", "adt"])
>>> p["tunable"]["epochs"]["default"]
30
See Also

mtb.run : takes these keys as params={method: {key: value}}.

docs.title: Environments (mtb.env)
docs.text:
Install the environments the methods run in. dry_run=True shows each environment's state and download size. The environments are linux-64 only: on macOS and Windows only the dry run works.

Name Summary mtb.env.install Install the environments a set of methods needs; Linux only. Details

On macOS and Windows, install raises an error that is both an OSError and a RuntimeError.

How the environment is entered describes how a run enters an environment, and GPU or CPU? the CPU and GPU builds.

docs.title: mtb.env.install
docs.text:
install(
    methods: list[str] | None = None,
    *,
    category: str | None = None,
    dry_run: bool = False,
    flavor: str = "auto",
    build: bool = False,
)

Install the environments a set of methods needs; Linux only.

Each env is unpacked from its published archive, or built from its lockfile where none is published. Installed envs are skipped.

PARAMETERS DESCRIPTION methods

Method ids to cover; None = every method of category, or every method.

type list[str] | None default None

category

vertical, diagonal, mosaic or cross: the methods to cover when methods is None.

type str | None default None

dry_run

True = install nothing and return each env's state and size.

type bool default False

flavor

'cpu', 'gpu' or 'auto' ('gpu' when an NVIDIA GPU is visible): the archive build of each env.

type str default 'auto'

build

True = build every env from its lockfile instead of unpacking the archive.

type bool default False

RETURNS DESCRIPTION DataFrame

One row per env, the env serving the most methods first: env, methods, state ('have', 'packed archive published', 'name taken' ... on a dry run; 'PACKED', 'BUILD' after an install), flavor ('cpu', 'gpu', or 'any' for one archive for both), archive_bytes (the download) and unpacked_bytes (on disk).

RAISES DESCRIPTION KeyError

Unknown method id, with a did-you-mean hint.

RuntimeError

A real install on a host that is not Linux, no conda where needed, or a failed build.

Examples

>>> import multibench as mtb
>>> mtb.env.install(["Matilda", "totalVI"], dry_run=True)
>>> mtb.env.install(category="vertical")

docs.title: Data I/O (mtb.io)
docs.text:
Write your data as a dataset folder the methods can read, and read its canonical .h5 files back. Give raw counts: the methods normalise the data themselves. A canonical .h5 holds one matrix as features x cells, the layout the methods read.

Name Summary mtb.io.export_dataset Write an AnnData / MuData (or loose objects) as a canonical dataset folder. mtb.io.read_canonical Read a canonical .h5 (a dataset file or an embedding.h5) as an AnnData.

docs.title: mtb.io.export_dataset
docs.text:
export_dataset(
    data,
    dataset_dir: Path | str,
    *,
    rna="X",
    adt=None,
    atac=None,
    atac_kind: str | None = None,
    labels=None,
    batch=None,
    category: str | None = None,
    adt_names: list | None = None,
    batch_index: int | None = None,
    overwrite: bool = False,
) -> Path

Write an AnnData / MuData (or loose objects) as a canonical dataset folder.

Produces the dataset folder layout (rna.h5, adt.h5, ATAC files, cty.csv), so mtb.scan and mtb.run work on your own data. Give raw counts. The files of each category are listed at https://dsichang.github.io/scMultiBench/tutorials/run/#folder-layout.

PARAMETERS DESCRIPTION data

Object the selector strings refer to; None when every modality is passed as an object. With a MuData, name each modality (rna='rna').

type (AnnData, MuData or None)

dataset_dir

Folder to create; its name is the dataset id for mtb.scan / mtb.run, and its parent their data_path.

type Path | str

rna

Raw-count matrix for RNA: a selector against data ('layer:counts', 'X[feature_types=Gene Expression]') or an AnnData, DataFrame or array; None = no RNA.

type (str, AnnData, DataFrame, array or None) default 'X'

adt

Raw-count matrix for protein (ADT), same forms as rna (e.g. 'obsm:protein'); None = no ADT.

type (str, AnnData, DataFrame, array or None) default None

atac

ATAC matrix, same forms as rna (e.g. 'X[feature_types=Peaks]'); None = no ATAC.

type (str, AnnData, DataFrame, array or None) default None

atac_kind

What atac holds: 'peak' or 'gene_activity'; decides the ATAC filename. None = read from the feature names: peaks (chr1:100-200) or the RNA's gene names.

type str or None default None

labels

Cell-type labels: a column, named 'obs:<col>' or '<col>' (a MuData's global .obs), '<mod>:<col>' (mdata[mod].obs), a Series indexed by barcode, or a sequence.

type (str, Series, sequence or None) default None

batch

Batch per cell, same forms as labels; splits the files per batch (rna1.h5, rna2.h5, ...) for mosaic or cross. Every cell needs a batch.

type (str, Series, sequence or None) default None

category

Integration category the folder is for (vertical, diagonal, mosaic or cross); sets the ATAC and label filenames.

type str or None default None

adt_names

Protein names for the ADT matrix; they override any it carries and are needed when it has none.

type list or None default None

batch_index

Write the whole object as batch N (rna<N>.h5, cty<N>.csv); mosaic, cross or diagonal in several batches, one call per batch.

type int or None default None

overwrite

True = replace files already in dataset_dir; False = raise before writing anything.

type bool default False

RETURNS DESCRIPTION Path

dataset_dir.

RAISES DESCRIPTION ValueError

Missing or conflicting arguments, a missing label or batch, or cells that do not pair across modalities.

KeyError

A selector names a mod, obsm, layer, obs or var column that is absent.

FileExistsError

A file this call would write exists and overwrite is False, or the folder holds files of other data.

WARNS DESCRIPTION UserWarning

Values that are not whole numbers, or feature names that are missing, repeated or contradict atac_kind.

Examples

>>> import multibench as mtb
>>> mtb.io.export_dataset(adata, "data/MYCITE", rna="layer:counts",
...                       adt="obsm:protein", labels="obs:celltype")
>>> mtb.io.export_dataset(mdata, "data/MYMULTIOME", rna="rna", atac="atac",
...                       atac_kind="peak", labels="obs:celltype",
...                       category="vertical")
See Also

mtb.scan : confirm the folder is found and which methods can run on it.

docs.title: mtb.io.read_canonical
docs.text:
read_canonical(path: Path | str)

Read a canonical .h5 (a dataset file or an embedding.h5) as an AnnData.

matrix/data (features x cells) becomes .X (cells x features, CSR when fewer than half of the entries are non-zero), matrix/features the var_names and matrix/barcodes the obs_names. A method's embedding.h5 goes to .obsm["X_emb"] of an AnnData without features.

PARAMETERS DESCRIPTION path

Canonical .h5 file.

type Path | str

RETURNS DESCRIPTION AnnData RAISES DESCRIPTION FileNotFoundError

path does not exist.

ValueError

path is a 10x Genomics .h5 file; the message says how to read it.

Examples

>>> import multibench as mtb
>>> rna = mtb.io.read_canonical(mtb.config.data_path / "D11" / "rna.h5")

docs.title: Plot (mtb.plot)
docs.text:
Draw figures from a long results table: mtb.load_results returns one for the stored results, mtb.evaluate and RunResult.long for your own runs. mtb.recommend(category, long_df=..., metrics=...) gives the numbers, in the row order of both figures with the same metrics.

Name Summary mtb.plot.bubble Draw the article's bubble table: methods as rows, metrics as columns. mtb.plot.bar Draw each method's overall score as a horizontal bar, best on top.

docs.title: mtb.plot.bubble
docs.text:
bubble(long_df, *, metrics=None, methods=None, title=None, save=None)

Draw the article's bubble table: methods as rows, metrics as columns.

Metrics are grouped into families, each led by an Overall bar. Rows run best first, in the order of mtb.recommend(category, long_df=long_df, metrics=...) with the same metrics.

PARAMETERS DESCRIPTION long_df

A long table (method, metric, value and optional dataset), as mtb.load_results, mtb.evaluate and RunResult.long return; stored and your own rows can be concatenated.

type DataFrame

metrics

A family ("clustering", "batch", "classification", "all"), a code, or codes in their column order; None = every metric in the frame.

type str, list of str | None default None

methods

Methods (rows) to show; None = every method in the frame.

type list of str | None default None

title

Figure title; None = "<category> <dataset>" when the table holds one of each; "" = no title.

type str | None default None

save

File to write the figure to; the suffix picks the format (.pdf, .png, .svg).

type str or path - like | None default None

RETURNS DESCRIPTION Figure RAISES DESCRIPTION ValueError

long_df lacks method / metric / value, repeats a (method, dataset, metric) row, holds your rows on another dataset than the stored rows, or metrics / methods names a value it does not hold.

WARNS DESCRIPTION UserWarning

n/a cells, several datasets averaged per method, a column with the same value in every row, or a figure of two methods.

Examples

>>> import multibench as mtb
>>> df = mtb.load_results("vertical", dataset="D11")
>>> fig = mtb.plot.bubble(df, metrics="clustering", save="d11.pdf")

docs.title: mtb.plot.bar
docs.text:
bar(
    long_df: DataFrame,
    *,
    metrics=None,
    methods=None,
    title: str | None = None,
    save: str | None = None,
)

Draw each method's overall score as a horizontal bar, best on top.

Within each dataset the methods are ranked on each metric; the bar is the across-dataset score, in the order of mtb.recommend(category, long_df=long_df, metrics=...) with the same metrics.

PARAMETERS DESCRIPTION long_df

A long table (method, metric, value and optional dataset), as mtb.load_results, mtb.evaluate and RunResult.long return.

type DataFrame

metrics

A family ("clustering", "batch", "classification", "all") drawn in its colour, a code, or codes; None = every metric.

type str, list of str | None default None

methods

Methods (bars) to show, ranked among themselves; None = every method in the frame.

type list of str | None default None

title

Figure title; None = the dataset, or the number of datasets.

type str | None default None

save

File to write the figure to.

type str | None default None

RETURNS DESCRIPTION Figure RAISES DESCRIPTION ValueError

long_df lacks method / metric / value, is empty, repeats a (method, dataset, metric) row, holds your rows on another dataset than the stored rows, or metrics / methods names a value it does not hold.

WARNS DESCRIPTION UserWarning

A method missing from some datasets, a dataset with one method, a metric only one method has, rows scored before 0.4.0, or a figure of two methods.

Examples

>>> import multibench as mtb
>>> df = mtb.load_results("diagonal")
>>> fig = mtb.plot.bar(df, metrics="clustering", save="clustering.png")

docs.title: Run
docs.text:
Run the methods of a category on a dataset folder and get their embeddings. Methods run only on Linux. On macOS and Windows, mtb.scan shows the plan and its commands.

Name Summary mtb.scan Check which methods can run on a dataset, and how run would run them. mtb.run Run the runnable methods of a category on a dataset folder, and score them. mtb.load_run Reload a saved run result. mtb.RunResult The result of mtb.run: its summary table, long table and figure.

docs.title: mtb.scan
docs.text:
scan(
    dataset: str,
    category: str | None = None,
    *,
    methods: list[str] | None = None,
    modalities: list[str] | str | None = None,
    params: dict | None = None,
    assume_gpu: bool = False,
    verbose: bool = True,
) -> DataFrame

Check which methods can run on a dataset, and how run would run them.

Nothing is executed and no file is written. Call it first on a new dataset: it prints what the folder holds and why each method that cannot run cannot.

PARAMETERS DESCRIPTION dataset

Dataset folder: its path, or its name under mtb.config.data_path.

type str

category

Integration category to scan; None = the benchmark's category of a dataset it scored (D11 is vertical), else all four.

type str | None default None

methods

Method ids to include, as a list; None = every method.

type list[str] | None default None

modalities

Modality tokens of one combination, e.g. ["rna", "adt"]; None = the combinations whose modalities the folder holds; "all" = every combination.

type list[str] | str | None default None

params

Hyperparameters per method, as run takes them; they are checked and appear in command.

type dict | None default None

assume_gpu

True = skip this host's GPU test, to check a job for a GPU node from a login node.

type bool default False

verbose

Print what the folder holds, the cells per file and each reason.

type bool default True

RETURNS DESCRIPTION DataFrame

One row per method (per method and category when category is None), runnable methods first: method, modalities (of the variant run would run, +-joined), runnable, reason (why it cannot run), env, caveat (what to know before running it) and command (the line run would execute, with <out_dir> for the output folder).

RAISES DESCRIPTION FileNotFoundError

The dataset folder does not exist; the message lists the folders present.

ValueError

Unknown category or modality token, or a method in methods without a variant there.

KeyError

Unknown method id, or a params key the method does not accept.

Examples

>>> import multibench as mtb
>>> mtb.scan("D11", "vertical")
>>> mtb.scan("data/MYCITE", "vertical", methods=["Matilda"],
...          params={"Matilda": {"epochs": 10}}).command[0]
See Also

mtb.run : runs the runnable methods.

docs.title: mtb.run
docs.text:
run(
    dataset: str,
    category: str,
    out_dir,
    *,
    methods=None,
    modalities=None,
    params: dict | None = None,
    batch=None,
    evaluate: bool = True,
    timeout: float | None = None,
    skip_existing: bool = False,
    verbose: bool = True,
) -> "RunResult"

Run the runnable methods of a category on a dataset folder, and score them.

Only the methods mtb.scan marks runnable run. A method's failure is recorded, never raised, and the results are saved under out_dir. methods=["Matilda"] runs one method. mtb.scan shows the plan first, with each command.

PARAMETERS DESCRIPTION dataset

Dataset folder: its path, or its name under mtb.config.data_path.

type str

category

Integration category: vertical, diagonal, mosaic or cross.

type str

out_dir

Output root, one <out_dir>/<method>_<dataset>/ per method. An embedding.h5 there also holds its cells' names (barcodes).

type path

methods

Method ids to run, as a list; None = every runnable method.

type list[str] | None default None

modalities

Modality tokens of one combination, e.g. ["rna", "adt"]; None = every combination the folder holds; "all" = every combination.

type list[str] | str | None default None

params

Hyperparameters per method, {"Matilda": {"epochs": 3}}; mtb.params_for lists the keys.

type dict | None default None

batch

One batch per cell; a Series or a barcode-indexed CSV is aligned by barcode. None = each cell's label file.

type array - like | Series | path | None default None

evaluate

Score each embedding; False only runs (status ran).

type bool default True

timeout

Wall-clock limit per method, in seconds; None = none.

type float | None default None

skip_existing

Reuse an output already in out_dir instead of running the method again, to resume an interrupted run.

type bool default False

verbose

Print [run] ... progress lines.

type bool default True

RETURNS DESCRIPTION RunResult

Read summary first, embedding(method) for an embedding.

RAISES DESCRIPTION FileNotFoundError

The dataset folder does not exist; the message lists the folders present.

ValueError

Nothing in the selection can run, an out_dir that holds the result of another dataset or category, or a batch that does not fit the cells; checked before anything runs.

KeyError

Unknown method id, or a params key the method does not accept.

Examples

>>> import multibench as mtb
>>> res = mtb.run("D11", "vertical", out_dir="out/")
>>> res = mtb.run("D11", "vertical", out_dir="out/", methods=["Matilda"],
...               params={"Matilda": {"epochs": 10}})

docs.title: mtb.load_run
docs.text:
load_run(out_dir, *, methods=None) -> 'RunResult'

Reload a saved run result.

PARAMETERS DESCRIPTION out_dir

A run out_dir: the folder holding batch_result.json.

type path - like

methods

Methods whose records to keep; None = every record.

type list[str] | None default None

RETURNS DESCRIPTION RunResult

The reloaded result; save() with no argument writes back to out_dir.

RAISES DESCRIPTION FileNotFoundError

out_dir holds no batch_result.json.

KeyError

A name in methods has no record; the message lists the methods that do.

WARNS DESCRIPTION UserWarning

The scores were made by multibench 0.3.x; res.rescore() scores them as 0.4.0 does.

Examples

>>> import multibench as mtb
>>> res = mtb.load_run("out/")
>>> res.summary
>>> mtb.load_run("out/", methods=["Matilda", "scMM"]).plot()
Notes

A copied run folder can be re-scored: each record's output folder is looked for next to batch_result.json when its recorded path is gone, and the dataset folder under the recorded data root, then mtb.config.data_path.

docs.title: mtb.RunResult
docs.text:
RunResult(records, dataset, category, out_dir=None)

The result of mtb.run: its summary table, long table and figure.

mtb.run and mtb.load_run build it. It keeps one record per method, which rescore and plot read.

PARAMETERS DESCRIPTION records

One record per method run, as run builds them.

type list[dict]

dataset

Dataset folder name the run used.

type str

category

Integration category of the run.

type str

out_dir

Where the run wrote its outputs; save() defaults to it.

type path | None default None

ATTRIBUTES DESCRIPTION records

One dict per method, as saved in batch_result.json: method, status (as in summary), out_dir (its output folder), params_used, run_sec, reused (True when skip_existing reused a saved output), metrics, labels_used (the label files in the cell order scored), error or note (the reason of summary) and the run's provenance (multibench_version, scripts_commit, env_flavor, hostname).

type list[dict]

dataset

Dataset folder name.

type str

category

Integration category.

type str

out_dir

The run's output root, or None for an in-memory result.

type path | None

Examples

>>> import multibench as mtb
>>> res = mtb.run("D11", "vertical", out_dir="out/", timeout=3600)
>>> res.summary[["method", "status", "ARI", "NMI"]]
>>> res.summary[res.summary.status != "scored"]   # what did not finish, and why
>>> fig = res.plot(metrics=["ARI", "NMI", "ASW"])
>>> res.rescore().save()                      # nothing re-run
Notes

len(res) is the number of method records.

See Also

mtb.run : produces one.

mtb.load_run : reloads one from save()'s folder.

mtb.plot.bubble : the figure plot draws from long.

docs.title: summary property
docs.text:
summary: DataFrame

One row per method: status, timing, label matching and every metric.

RETURNS DESCRIPTION DataFrame

One row per method, sorted by method:

method                  method id
status                  scored, ran, failed, skipped or timeout
ARI, NMI, ASW, ...      one column per metric
run_sec                 seconds of the method run
caveat                  scan's caveat for the method, or ""
reason                  why the method has no scores, or ""

Examples

>>> res = mtb.load_run("out/")
>>> res.summary[["method", "status", "ARI"]]
See Also

mtb.load_run : reads a saved folder; its batch_result.json holds every record, with the label orders tried.

docs.title: long property
docs.text:
long: DataFrame

The scores as a long table, for plotting.

This is what plot and mtb.plot.bubble consume.

RETURNS DESCRIPTION DataFrame

Columns metric, value, method, dataset, category and source. When the scores carry scored_with, so does the table. Empty, with the first six columns, when no method produced metrics.

Examples

>>> res = mtb.load_run("out/")
>>> mtb.plot.bubble(res.long, metrics=["ARI", "NMI"])
>>> res.long.pivot_table(index="method", columns="metric", values="value")
Notes

Source of the rows. Each record contributes the unrounded frame run attached (or long.csv via mtb.load_run) when present. Otherwise the record contributes its metrics dict.

See Also

RunResult.plot : draws the bubble figure from this frame.

docs.title: plot
docs.text:
plot(**kw)

Bubble figure of every method that produced metrics.

Rows are methods, best first. Circle size shows the rank within a column (bigger is better). Fill compares the values in a column: the lightest is the lowest in this figure, not zero.

PARAMETERS DESCRIPTION **kw

Keyword arguments of mtb.plot.bubble: metrics=, methods=, title= and save=.

default {}

RETURNS DESCRIPTION Figure

Save it with fig.savefig("out.png").

RAISES DESCRIPTION ValueError

Nothing was scored (summary says why), or an unknown name in methods=.

Examples

>>> res = mtb.load_run("out/")
>>> fig = res.plot()
>>> fig = res.plot(metrics=["ARI", "NMI", "ASW"], title="D11 vertical")
>>> fig.savefig("D11_vertical.png", dpi=200)
Notes

Keywords. metrics= sets the column order and methods= a subset. There is no default title: pass title= when one is wanted.

Reading the figure. Size and colour are relative to the methods in this figure, so with few methods a small gap fills the whole colour scale. Check the values in summary.

See Also

mtb.plot.bubble : the underlying function and its full keyword list.

RunResult.long : the frame handed to it.

docs.title: rescore
docs.text:
rescore(
    *, batch=None, labels=None, metrics=None, verbose: bool = True
) -> "RunResult"

Score the saved outputs again with new labels, batch or metrics.

No method is re-run. Each record's embedding is read back from its out_dir. The Leiden clusters depend on the cell order and the machine, so the same embedding can score a few hundredths differently.

PARAMETERS DESCRIPTION batch

Batch ids in the order of the dataset's label files, or a barcode-indexed Series or CSV. Every cell needs a batch. None = the batch run was given, else each cell's label file.

type array - like | Series | path | None default None

labels

One cell-type label per cell; a Series or a barcode-indexed CSV is aligned by barcode. None = the dataset's label files, in the order the record was scored with (ranked as run ranks them when it has none).

type array - like | Series | path | None default None

metrics

Metric family ("clustering", "batch", "classification", "all") or metric codes, which replace those scores and keep the others; None = every metric the batch structure allows, as in mtb.evaluate.

type str | list[str] | None default None

verbose

Print one line per method, and one before each label-order ranking.

type bool default True

RETURNS DESCRIPTION RunResult

A new result; this one is untouched. Call .save(out_dir) on it to persist it.

RAISES DESCRIPTION FileNotFoundError

The output of no method is found; the message gives the first method's error. A method that cannot be scored otherwise gets the status ran, and reason says why.

ValueError

labels or batch holds ids that are not cells of the dataset, or a cell has no batch.

FileNotFoundError

labels or batch is the name of an obs column, such as "donor". Pass the column itself: batch=adata.obs["donor"].

WARNS DESCRIPTION UserWarning

A Series or barcode-indexed CSV cannot be aligned and is matched by position.

Examples

>>> mtb.load_run("out/").rescore().save()
See Also

mtb.evaluate : the scoring function applied per record. RunResult.save : persist the re-scored result.

docs.title: embedding
docs.text:
embedding(method: str)

The embedding of one method, as an AnnData.

PARAMETERS DESCRIPTION method

A method of this result.

type str

RETURNS DESCRIPTION AnnData

obsm["X_emb"] in the method's cell order; obs_names are the cells' barcodes, each prefixed by its label file (cty2:AAAC...) when some barcode is in two files; obs holds each cell's label, and its batch when the run had more than one batch.

RAISES DESCRIPTION KeyError

No record for method.

ValueError

The method did not run, or it writes a graph instead of an embedding.

FileNotFoundError

Its output folder is gone.

Examples

>>> res = mtb.run("D11", "vertical", methods=["Matilda"], out_dir="out/")
>>> adata = res.embedding("Matilda")
>>> sc.pp.neighbors(adata, use_rep="X_emb")

docs.title: save
docs.text:
save(out_dir=None) -> 'Path'

Write this result to disk so it outlives the process.

PARAMETERS DESCRIPTION out_dir

Target folder, created if missing; None = the result's own out_dir, else the current directory.

type path | None default None

RETURNS DESCRIPTION Path

The folder written.

RAISES DESCRIPTION ValueError

The folder holds a saved result of another dataset or category.

Examples

>>> res = mtb.load_run("out/")
>>> res.rescore(metrics="clustering").save("out/clustering_only")
>>> mtb.load_run("out/clustering_only").summary
Notes

Files written.

  • summary.csv - the summary frame.
  • long.csv - the long frame, only when some method produced metrics.
  • batch_result.json - dataset, category and the per-method records.
  • batch_<hash>.csv - a batch vector the records were scored with.

Saving into a folder that has a result. When the folder already holds batch_result.json for the same dataset and category, the records are merged. A method in this result replaces its earlier record, unless its status is skipped and the earlier one's is not; the other earlier records are kept, every file in the list above is rewritten from the merged set, and a line [save] Merged with 1 earlier record in <folder> (StabMap). names them. This result object is not changed. Jobs running at the same time should use one out_dir each; combine their long tables with pandas.concat to plot them together.

See Also

mtb.load_run : reads the folder back.

docs.title: Score
docs.text:
Score an embedding with the article's metrics. The scores come as the long table that mtb.load_results returns. The API overview summarises the metrics= selector.

Name Summary mtb.evaluate Score an embedding with the benchmark's metrics.

docs.title: mtb.evaluate
docs.text:
evaluate(
    embedding,
    labels=None,
    *,
    dataset: str | None = None,
    method: str = "embedding",
    category: str | None = None,
    batch=None,
    metrics=None,
    obsm: str | None = None,
    verbose: bool = True,
) -> DataFrame

Score an embedding with the benchmark's metrics.

The protocol is the article's: Leiden clusters searched to the number of cell types for ARI, NMI, ASW, iASW and iF1, and to the number of batches for ARI_batch and NMI_batch.

PARAMETERS DESCRIPTION embedding

Cells x dims: an array, DataFrame, AnnData or MuData (.obsm[obsm]), or a file: .h5 (the benchmark's embedding.h5), .h5ad, .npy, .csv / .tsv.

labels

One cell type per cell: CSV path(s), a 1-D array-like, or an .obs column name ("celltype", "rna:celltype" for a MuData modality). None = the label files of dataset.

default None

dataset

The dataset folder, a name or a path; its name fills the dataset column. With labels=None its label files are read and matched to the cells by the names run writes into embedding.h5; for a file of a run folder without them, in the cell order of the method its run record names; else in the order of method when that is a package method.

type str | None default None

method

Fills the method column: a package method id or your own name.

type str default 'embedding'

category

vertical, diagonal, mosaic or cross; fills the category column. With two or more batches, all but vertical add the classification metrics.

type str | None default None

batch

One batch per cell, in the forms labels takes; needed for the batch metrics unless labels lists two or more files.

default None

metrics

None = every metric the inputs allow except kBET; a family ("clustering", "batch", "classification", "all"), a code ("ARI") or a list of codes and families.

type None, str or list of str default None

obsm

.obsm key of an AnnData, MuData or .h5ad embedding; 'X' means .X. None = X_emb.

type str | None default None

verbose

Print a line when the Leiden search starts on more than 2,000 cells or labels are matched by barcode.

type bool default True

RETURNS DESCRIPTION DataFrame

The long table: metric, value, method, dataset, category, source, scored_with, one row per metric. mtb.plot.bubble draws it, next to mtb.load_results rows or alone.

RAISES DESCRIPTION ValueError

Missing or misaligned labels or batches, an unknown category or metric, or batch or classification metrics without batch labels.

FileNotFoundError

An embedding, label file or dataset folder that does not exist.

Examples

>>> import multibench as mtb
>>> mtb.evaluate("out/Matilda_D11/embedding.h5", dataset="D11",
...              category="vertical", method="Matilda")
>>> mtb.evaluate(adata, labels="celltype", batch="sample", obsm="X_pca",
...              method="PCA")

docs.title: Cross integration: Multiple ADT + ATAC¶
docs.text:
Cross integration combines batches that all measure the same modalities. The task is to remove batch effects and keep the biological structure. This tutorial is for batches that each hold ADT and ATAC peaks, with no RNA. It runs StabMap and UINMF on D58mini, 3,000 cells in two batches of the benchmark dataset D58, and then on data in your own format.

Methods run on Linux. On macOS or Windows, open this notebook in Colab.

docs.title: 1. Install¶
docs.text:
This cell installs multibench-sc. It keeps the numpy and pandas that are already installed, so Colab needs no restart.

Details

On Colab, choose a GPU runtime before you run the notebook: Runtime -> Change runtime type -> T4 GPU. On a CPU runtime, an environment that has a smaller CPU build gets that build, and training methods run slower.

docs.title: 2. Download the data and the environments¶
docs.text:
mtb.data.fetch downloads D58mini (7 MB) once. Each method runs in its own environment. mtb.env.install downloads the environments for StabMap and UINMF, with no conda needed. The download is 0.9 GB.

Details

state is PACKED for an environment downloaded now and have for one that was already there. With dry_run=True, mtb.env.install downloads nothing and returns the plan with its sizes.

Environments go to mtb.config.envs_dir. To use another disk, set it before this cell.

docs.title: 3. Run the methods¶
docs.text:
run runs each method on D58mini and scores its output with the scIB metrics and the classification scores (OCA, ACA, Spec, Sens, F1). res.summary has one row per method with its status, run time and scores. Higher is better for every metric.

Details

Each method writes an embedding: a table of numbers with one row per cell. run scores it against the cell-type labels of D58mini.

The clustering metrics ARI, NMI, ASW, iASW, iF1 and cLISI measure how well the embedding separates the cell types. The batch metrics ASW_batch, ARI_batch, NMI_batch, GC and iLISI measure how well the batches mix. They appear only when the data has several batches.

The reason column of res.summary says why a method failed. params={"Method": {"key": value}} sets a method's parameters, and mtb.params_for lists them. Many methods take none.

mtb.load_run("out/D58mini") reloads these results later without running anything.

docs.title: 4. Plot¶
docs.text:
res.plot() draws the scores as a bubble table. Circle size shows the rank within a column, and bigger is better. The fill compares a value with the other rows in the same column.

Details

The lightest fill is the lowest value in this figure, not zero.

Metrics are grouped by family: blue for clustering, green for batch correction, pink for classification. Each family starts with an Overall bar. Its length and colour both show the family score.

A column whose rows all hold the same value is drawn grey, and a warning names it. A figure of one method is grey everywhere.

docs.title: 5. Your own data¶
docs.text:
Your data needs raw ADT counts in one .h5ad file and an ATAC peak matrix of the same cells in another, with a cell type and a batch for each cell. ADT means the protein counts. A batch is a donor, a sample or an experiment. mtb.io.export_dataset with batch= writes one set of files per batch. rna=None says that the data has no RNA.

The methods of this task read two batches. The recipe for another number of donors covers the other cases.

Starting from something else? See the recipes for a 10x .h5 file, labels in a CSV file, no labels and another number of donors.

Details: export

The names in quotes say where your file holds each part. "X" is the main matrix, "obsm:protein" the matrix obsm["protein"], "layer:counts" the layer layers["counts"], and "obs:celltype" the column obs["celltype"], which "celltype" alone names too. A wrong name after obsm:, layer: or obs: raises an error that lists the names the file has.

When the ADT file also holds a matrix in obsm under a name that does not start with X_, export_dataset asks which one is the protein matrix. X_umap and X_pca are left alone.

The batches are numbered in the sorted order of their names, read as text: donors A, B and C become batches 1, 2 and 3, and 10 comes before 2.

For one AnnData per batch, call export_dataset once per batch with batch_index=N instead of batch=.

"mydata/" + NAME is the dataset folder that scan and run read. With a new value of NAME, the folder holds the files of your data only.

The check lists the methods you name. Without methods=, it lists every method that reads the modalities in the folder. Its command column holds the line run would execute for each method.

export_dataset raises FileExistsError when the folder holds files of other cells that the call does not write. overwrite=True does not remove them. Give NAME a new value. After batch=, the files of batch numbers that the call does not write count as well.

overwrite=True replaces the files of an earlier run of this cell. Without it, export_dataset raises FileExistsError rather than replace a file.
